content:
Loneliness has been linked to changes in the brain that can alter alcohol‑drinking behavior, a new preclinical study from Northwestern University and the Salk Institute for Biological Studies reports. The research, published in a peer‑reviewed journal, identifies a specific neural pathway that mediates how social isolation influences alcohol consumption in mice.

The investigators found that isolation increases drinking in male mice while paradoxically reducing it in females. By mapping the circuitry involved, the team demonstrated that the brain’s response to loneliness is sex‑specific, with distinct mechanisms driving the divergent patterns of alcohol use. These findings provide the first mechanistic insight into how social deprivation can differentially affect substance use across sexes.

The study’s authors suggest that the identified pathway could serve as a target for future interventions aimed at mitigating alcohol misuse, especially in populations experiencing chronic loneliness. Further research will be needed to determine whether similar mechanisms operate in humans and how they might inform tailored prevention strategies.
author: Medical Xpress

title: DR Congo and M23 Rebels Agree to Restart Peace Talks
content:
Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo’s volatile east remains under the sway of Rwanda‑backed M23 rebels, who continue to hold extensive swaths of territory despite ongoing government offensives. The insurgents, who seized key towns earlier this year, have been a persistent obstacle to stability in the region, prompting international concern and a series of stalled negotiations aimed at a cease‑fire and political settlement.

After months of deadlocked talks, representatives of the Congolese government and M23 commanders announced a renewed commitment to resume dialogue, pledging to “get the ball rolling again” in hopes of de‑escalating the conflict. The announcement, reported by France 24’s Emmet Livingstone from Kinshasa, signals a tentative step toward a negotiated solution, though the durability of the renewed talks will depend on both parties’ willingness to adhere to agreed terms and on continued diplomatic engagement.
author: France 24

title: Pakistan Reports Progress in Iran-US War Talks
content:
Pakistan’s army chief and interior minister conducted a series of talks in Tehran during a daylong diplomatic mission to the Iranian capital. The meetings were held as part of the officials’ broader engagement with Iranian counterparts, aiming to advance bilateral cooperation on a range of issues.

The discussions took place amid a schedule that included meetings with senior Iranian security and political leaders, as well as visits to key diplomatic sites. The agenda focused on strengthening military-to-military ties, coordinating border security efforts, and exploring avenues for joint initiatives in regional stability.

The mission concluded with a joint statement affirming the commitment of both countries to deepen cooperation and maintain open channels of communication. The talks are expected to lay the groundwork for future collaborative projects and reinforce the diplomatic relationship between Pakistan and Iran.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Nvidia and Supermicro employees indicted for illegal AI server exports to China
content:
Taiwanese prosecutors have formally charged nine individuals in connection with an alleged scheme to smuggle advanced semiconductor components out of the island, according to a statement released by the Taipei District Prosecutors Office on Friday. The indictment cites violations of the country's export control regulations, which are designed to prevent the unauthorized transfer of high‑technology products that could have national security implications. Authorities say the suspects, who include former employees of a local chip manufacturer and several logistics operators, coordinated the illicit shipment of micro‑chips through falsified customs documents and concealed packaging.

Investigators uncovered the operation during a months‑long probe that began after customs officials flagged irregularities in cargo declarations at Kaohsiung Port. The case underscores Taiwan’s heightened vigilance over its semiconductor sector, a critical pillar of the national economy and a focal point of global supply‑chain security concerns. The nine defendants face charges that could result in substantial fines and imprisonment if convicted, and the prosecution has indicated that further inquiries may identify additional parties involved in the network.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kenya nurses strike over pay and working conditions
content:
Nurses across Kenya have entered a nationwide strike, demanding fair wages and improved working conditions, with Shiru Kihara, a registered nurse from Nairobi, speaking on behalf of the thousands of health workers involved. The industrial action, which began on Monday, follows months of stalled negotiations between the Kenya Nurses Union and the Ministry of Health over salary increments that union leaders say have not kept pace with inflation and the rising cost of living. Kihara highlighted that many nurses receive salaries that are insufficient to cover basic expenses, leading to increased stress and a decline in morale among frontline staff.

The strike has prompted the Ministry of Health to acknowledge the concerns and announce a series of round‑table meetings aimed at reaching a settlement within the next two weeks. While hospitals continue to operate with reduced staffing, emergency services remain functional, and the government has urged the public to seek care at designated facilities to avoid disruptions. Union representatives, including Kihara, have indicated that a resolution will depend on a concrete pay raise and commitments to address workload and safety issues, underscoring the broader challenge of retaining qualified nurses in Kenya’s public health system.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Land restoration sparks job creation for young entrepreneurs
content:
A growing cohort of entrepreneurs across the globe is turning land restoration into a viable source of income, according to a United Nations‑backed initiative. From Ecuadorian farms repurposing agricultural waste into bio‑fuel and compost, to Bangladeshi start‑ups installing AI‑powered soil sensors in rice paddies, these innovators are demonstrating that ecological rehabilitation can coexist with profitable business models. The program, which partners with local governments and private investors, offers technical training, access to low‑cost financing and a platform for sharing best practices, enabling participants to scale their projects while improving soil health and biodiversity.

The initiative’s early results suggest a win‑win for communities and the planet. In Ecuador, a pilot greenhouse network has increased crop yields by 15% while reducing water use by 20%, generating a new revenue stream for smallholder farmers. In Bangladesh, sensor‑driven irrigation has cut fertilizer waste by 30%, boosting farmers’ margins and reducing runoff pollution. As the program expands, it aims to create a global network of land‑restoration entrepreneurs who can replicate these models, proving that environmental stewardship and economic development can be mutually reinforcing.
author: UN News

title: Federer confirms US Open exhibition match, no comeback plans
content:
Roger Federer, the 20‑time Grand Slam champion, has confirmed that he will not return to competitive tennis after a brief stint in an exhibition match. The Swiss legend, who has been a dominant force in the sport for over two decades, announced the decision during a press briefing at the Swiss Open in Gstaad, stating that the exhibition match will be his final appearance on the professional circuit.

Federer’s announcement follows his retirement announcement earlier this year, in which he cited a desire to preserve his legacy and focus on family. The exhibition match, scheduled for the opening weekend of the 2026 season, will feature a limited field of top players and is intended as a farewell event rather than a competitive comeback. The tennis community has largely welcomed the decision, noting that it allows Federer to close his illustrious career on his own terms.

With the exhibition match set to take place in Gstaad, fans and commentators alike will be watching to see how the former world No. 1 concludes his storied career. The event is expected to draw significant attention, offering a final glimpse of Federer’s skill and sportsmanship before he fully steps away from the sport.
author: Al Jazeera

title: India pledge to bar ousted Bangladeshi PM from politics could ease bilateral deadlock
content:
Analysts say that a formal Indian pledge to bar the ousted former prime minister of Bangladesh from conducting political activities on Indian soil could ease the country’s fraught political climate. The move, they argue, would reduce the likelihood of the ex‑leader using India as a base to influence domestic politics and would signal a clear stance on respecting Bangladesh’s sovereign processes.

The suggestion comes amid heightened tensions between Bangladesh’s ruling party and its opposition, which has repeatedly accused the government of undermining democratic norms. By refusing to allow the former prime minister to campaign or mobilize supporters in India, the country would not only limit cross‑border political interference but also reinforce the integrity of Bangladesh’s electoral system. Experts note that such a commitment would strengthen diplomatic ties, as it demonstrates India’s willingness to support Bangladesh’s internal stability without imposing overt political pressure.

While the proposal has not yet been formalized, it reflects a broader trend of regional actors seeking to contain political spill‑over. If adopted, the pledge could help calm domestic unrest in Bangladesh and reinforce the principle that political engagement should remain within a nation’s borders, thereby contributing to a more predictable and peaceful political environment in the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Thai vendor confronts Israeli tourists with Palestinian flag in Phuket
content:
A Thai street vendor on Phuket’s Patong Beach confronted a group of Israeli tourists outside his stall on Monday, brandishing a Palestinian flag and demanding that they leave the premises. The encounter, which was captured on video and quickly spread on social media, showed the vendor waving the flag and speaking in Thai while the tourists appeared startled but did not engage in a physical altercation. Local police arrived shortly after the incident was reported, separating the parties and taking statements from both the vendor and the visitors.

The episode reflects heightened tensions worldwide following the recent escalation of the Israel‑Palestine conflict, which has prompted demonstrations and confrontations in several tourist destinations. Phuket authorities confirmed that the vendor will face a routine investigation for possible harassment, while tourism officials emphasized that the island remains a safe destination for all visitors. No injuries were reported, and the Israeli tourists continued their stay after the matter was resolved.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Global ocean temperatures reach record high as El Niño intensifies
content:
The European Union’s Copernicus Climate Change Service has issued an alert that the world’s oceans are experiencing “unprecedented strain” as a combination of a strong El Niño event and ongoing climate‑change‑driven warming pushes sea‑surface temperatures to record levels. Satellite observations and in‑situ measurements compiled by Copernicus show global ocean temperatures rising faster than in any comparable period of the past several decades, with several regions already registering marine heatwaves that exceed historical norms. The agency attributes the surge to the simultaneous impact of the current El Niño, which typically raises temperatures in the Pacific and adjacent basins, and the long‑term upward trend caused by greenhouse‑gas emissions.

The elevated temperatures are expected to intensify stress on marine ecosystems, including increased coral bleaching, shifts in fish distribution, and heightened risk of hypoxic zones that can affect commercial fisheries and biodiversity. Copernicus emphasizes that continued monitoring and rapid mitigation efforts are essential to limit further oceanic degradation and to safeguard the services the oceans provide to global food security and climate regulation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Rohingya refugees protest in Bangladesh nine years after exodus
content:
Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh’s sprawling camps near Cox’s Bazar staged a coordinated protest on Tuesday, marking the ninth anniversary of the mass exodus that forced more than 700,000 people to flee violence in Myanmar’s Rakhine State. Organized by community leaders and supported by several humanitarian groups, the demonstration featured chants and placards calling for accelerated repatriation, improved living conditions, and greater access to education and livelihood opportunities within the camps. Authorities reported that around 2,000 participants gathered at the main camp entrance, while security forces maintained a presence to ensure order and prevent clashes.

Bangladeshi officials reiterated their commitment to a voluntary, safe return of the Rohingya, emphasizing ongoing diplomatic efforts with Myanmar and the United Nations to secure guarantees of citizenship and security for returnees. The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) welcomed the peaceful nature of the protest but warned that funding shortfalls and stalled negotiations could prolong the displacement. As the anniversary approaches, international donors are being urged to increase assistance, while the Rohingya community remains focused on securing a durable solution to their protracted plight.
author: Al Jazeera

title: ‘There was a lot of doubt and pain’: Arthur Fery on his dream Wimbledon run and the next step
content:
British No 2 Arthur Fery reflected on his rapid rise and current challenges ahead of his US Open debut, describing his journey as a “Fery‑tale”. A year ago the 24‑year‑old was ranked around 300 and battling a persistent arm injury, yet he surged to the Wimbledon semi‑finals, a performance that propelled him to world No 36. The unexpected run, which included five consecutive victories, was hailed as a remarkable turnaround in his career and earned him a place among Britain’s top players.

Speaking in Cincinnati, Fery acknowledged the contrast between the euphoria of Wimbledon and the ongoing physical setbacks he faces. While the injury has caused periods of doubt, he said his self‑belief remains strong and he is focused on consolidating his ranking ahead of the US Open. The British No 2 aims to build on his recent success, maintain his position within the top‑50 and establish a more consistent presence on the ATP Tour.
author: Guardian Sport

title: French Language Sparks Tension in US-Canada Trade War
content:
The trade dispute between the United States and Canada has intensified after President Donald Trump announced new tariffs, following a series of failed negotiations. The conflict now extends beyond economic demands, with linguistic concerns emerging as a significant point of contention.  

Prime Minister Mark Carney has warned that Washington’s stance threatens the status of French in Canada, a nation that officially recognizes both English and French. Carney’s remarks highlight that the dispute is not solely about tariff levels but also about perceived threats to the bilingual framework that has long been a cornerstone of Canadian policy and identity.  

The Canadian government has reiterated its commitment to protecting the French language while seeking a resolution to the tariff escalation. As negotiations continue, the linguistic dimension remains a politically sensitive issue that could influence the broader outcome of the trade talks.
author: France 24

title: US imposes 50% tariffs on select Canadian goods, Canada to respond
content:
Canada announced it will take action in response to President Donald Trump’s decision to impose new tariffs on Tuesday, marking a sharp escalation in the trade dispute between the two North American neighbors. The tariffs, set at 50 percent on a range of Canadian products, were introduced after Ottawa and Washington failed to reach an agreement on Friday that could have avoided the measure.

The U.S. administration cited concerns over Canadian dairy and lumber exports as the basis for the tariffs, while Canadian officials criticized the move as a violation of trade agreements and a threat to the long‑standing economic partnership. Ottawa has indicated it will explore retaliatory measures and will engage with allies and international trade bodies to address the impact on Canadian businesses and consumers.

The development underscores a growing trade war that threatens to disrupt supply chains and economic stability in both countries. Canadian authorities are preparing to negotiate a response while monitoring the potential ramifications for bilateral trade and regional markets.
author: France 24

title: Chelsea beat Fulham 3-2 in Xabi Alonso's managerial debut
content:
Chelsea earned a 3‑2 Premier League win over Fulham on Saturday, providing a victorious start for new manager Xabi Alonso in his first competitive match at the helm. The home side took the lead through a first‑half strike before Fulham equalised, and the game remained level until late in the second half when Chelsea secured the decisive goals to clinch all three points at Stamford Bridge.  

The result moves Chelsea up the league table and gives Alonso an immediate boost as he begins his tenure, while Fulham remain in the mid‑table zone after the narrow defeat. Both clubs will look to build on the performance as the season progresses.
author: France 24

title: Iran conflict spurs cyber attacks on critical infrastructure
content:
Recent attacks in both the United Kingdom and the United States have highlighted critical vulnerabilities in national security infrastructure, prompting officials to call for immediate remedial action. Authorities in the UK reported a series of coordinated incidents that targeted public services, while U.S. agencies disclosed breaches affecting multiple sectors, including energy and transportation. Both governments have described the events as a stark reminder of the evolving threat landscape and have emphasized the need to reassess existing protective measures.

In response, senior officials in London and Washington have outlined plans to strengthen cyber‑defence capabilities, enhance inter‑agency coordination, and allocate additional resources toward resilience programs. Legislative bodies are expected to review current policies, and security agencies are conducting comprehensive risk assessments to identify gaps. The coordinated focus on addressing these vulnerabilities underscores a shared commitment to safeguarding critical infrastructure and public safety against future attacks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Partial Lunar Eclipse on 28 August Turns Moon Red over UK
content:
A partial lunar eclipse will be visible from the United Kingdom on Saturday, 28 August, with the Moon expected to take on a reddish hue as it passes through the Earth’s shadow. The eclipse will begin at 02:12 UTC, reaching maximum coverage at 04:45 UTC, and will conclude around 07:18 UTC. Observers in the UK will see the eclipse in the early morning hours, with the event most prominent over the western and northern parts of the country.

During a partial lunar eclipse, only a portion of the Moon enters the Earth’s umbra, the darkest part of its shadow. The remaining portion remains illuminated by reflected sunlight, creating a characteristic “blood‑red” appearance when the Moon is partially obscured. This reddish coloration results from the Earth’s atmosphere scattering shorter wavelengths of light and allowing longer‑wavelength reds and oranges to reach the Moon. The eclipse is expected to be visible to the public across the UK, offering a clear demonstration of celestial mechanics and atmospheric scattering.

Astronomers advise that the eclipse can be safely observed with the naked eye, binoculars, or a telescope. The event provides an excellent opportunity for amateur astronomers and the general public to witness a natural astronomical phenomenon, while also highlighting the interplay between Earth’s atmosphere and the Moon’s illumination.
author: BBC Science

title: Omega Launches Mini Moonwatch Collection
content:
A new line of 38‑mm Speedmaster watches has been introduced, offering a refreshed take on the classic chronograph. The updated models retain the iconic round case and signature tachymeter bezel while incorporating contemporary design touches such as slimmer bezels, updated dial layouts, and refined finishing on the case and bracelet.

Each watch in the collection is powered by the same reliable automatic movement that has defined the Speedmaster for decades, but the new versions feature improved power reserve and enhanced water resistance. The 38‑mm case size strikes a balance between the traditional 42‑mm models and the newer 36‑mm variants, appealing to wearers who prefer a more compact yet still substantial presence on the wrist.

The launch positions the Speedmaster as a versatile chronograph for both everyday wear and special occasions, continuing the brand’s legacy of precision and style while adapting to modern preferences.
author: Wired

title: London and Paris Illuminate Blue and Yellow for Ukraine’s 35th Independence Day
content:
London and Paris illuminated the night sky in blue and yellow to honour Ukraine’s 35th Independence Day. In London, the House of Commons and the Palace of Westminster were bathed in the Ukrainian flag’s colours, while the iconic Eiffel Tower in Paris mirrored the display, casting a patriotic glow over the Seine.  

The coordinated light‑up was organised by local authorities and Ukrainian community groups, aiming to show solidarity with Kyiv amid ongoing conflict. The choice of blue and yellow—Ukraine’s national colours—was intended to raise awareness of the country’s struggle for sovereignty and to celebrate its cultural identity.  

The events, which attracted large crowds and international media coverage, underscored the enduring diplomatic ties between the UK, France and Ukraine. Both capitals used the opportunity to reaffirm support for Ukraine’s independence and to highlight the shared values of democracy and resilience.
author: Euronews

title: Colombia's New President Orders Immigration Raids, Promises Deportations of Undocumented Migrants
content:
A Colombian far‑right politician who has long been a vocal ally of former U.S. President Donald Trump made headlines on Thursday after repeating a slogan that echoes the former president’s “America first” rhetoric. Speaking at a public rally in Bogotá, the leader—whose name is not disclosed in this report—declared, “Colombians first, Colombians second, Colombians third, may that be clear to everyone.” The statement was delivered in a tone that many observers noted mirrored Trump’s emphasis on prioritizing national interests over international cooperation.

The remarks come amid growing scrutiny of the politician’s close ties to Trump’s administration, which included shared positions on immigration, trade, and foreign policy. Analysts say the leader’s use of the slogan is intended to rally domestic support and signal a shift toward a more nationalist agenda. While the statement was met with applause from his supporters, it also drew criticism from opposition parties, who warned that such rhetoric could undermine Colombia’s diplomatic relations and domestic cohesion. The leader’s comments are likely to influence the political discourse in the run‑up to the upcoming national elections.
author: Euronews

title: Trial delayed for Libyan accused in 1988 Lockerbie bombing
content:
On August 21, 1988, a bomb detonated in the rear cargo hold of Pan Am Flight 103 as it flew over the Scottish town of Lockerbie. The explosion tore the aircraft apart, killing all 259 passengers and crew aboard and sending a shockwave that struck the ground, killing 11 residents of the town. The incident remains the deadliest terrorist attack in British history.

Investigations traced the device to a suitcase that had been loaded onto the flight in Frankfurt, with the bomb’s explosive charge engineered to rupture the fuselage at cruising altitude. The blast produced a massive fireball that collapsed the aircraft into the airspace above Lockerbie, while the resulting debris field and shrapnel caused the ground casualties. The attack prompted a worldwide manhunt and led to the eventual indictment of individuals linked to the Libyan government, who were accused of orchestrating the bombing.

The tragedy left an enduring legacy in both the United Kingdom and the United States, prompting changes in aviation security protocols and the establishment of memorials at the crash site. The Lockerbie case remains a stark reminder of the far-reaching impact of terrorism on civilian life and international aviation safety.
author: Euronews

title: Tornado Rips Through Pomas, France, Injuring 31
content:
A tornado tore through the small commune of Pomas in the Aude department of southern France, striking homes and roofs and leaving 31 people injured. The violent wind event unfolded as part of a broader outbreak of severe thunderstorms that have battered the region in recent hours.

Emergency services were dispatched immediately to the affected area, where first‑aid teams treated the injured and began securing damaged structures. Local authorities have opened a damage assessment and are coordinating with national meteorological agencies to investigate the tornado’s path and intensity. Residents reported that the storm brought sudden, high‑velocity winds that caused widespread structural damage before dissipating.

Officials are monitoring the situation as additional weather reports indicate that the storm system may still pose a threat to nearby towns. The Aude region remains on alert while authorities work to provide aid and restore services to the impacted communities.
author: Euronews

title: French language factor cited in US-Canada trade dispute after talks collapse
content:
The United States and Canada have seen their long‑standing trade negotiations collapse, turning a dispute over tariffs and market access into a broader cultural confrontation. After weeks of talks aimed at resolving lingering issues over dairy, lumber, and automotive parts, the two sides failed to reach a compromise last week, prompting both governments to reassert their positions on national sovereignty and economic policy.

The breakdown has amplified tensions on multiple fronts. U.S. officials have cited concerns over Canadian subsidies and market‑access restrictions, while Canadian leaders emphasize the need to protect domestic industries and maintain fair trade practices. The dispute now intersects with domestic political narratives, with each side framing the other’s policies as an attack on national identity and economic independence. Trade experts warn that prolonged standoffs could disrupt supply chains and increase costs for consumers in both countries.

In the absence of a negotiated settlement, Washington and Ottawa are likely to pursue alternative measures, including the imposition of retaliatory tariffs and the exploration of bilateral trade agreements with third‑party partners. The situation underscores the fragility of North American trade relations and the potential for economic disputes to evolve into broader ideological battles.
author: France 24

title: Australian charts ban AI-generated songs but allow AI-supported tracks
content:
The Official Charts Company announced that songs incorporating artificial‑intelligence technology will remain eligible for the UK singles and albums charts, provided the AI is used only in a “supporting role.” The clarification follows recent industry debate over how AI‑generated content should be classified, with the company emphasizing that the core creative contribution must still come from human artists, songwriters, or producers.

Under the new guidance, AI may be employed for tasks such as vocal enhancement, instrument synthesis, or lyric assistance, but the final composition must be principally human‑driven. Tracks that rely entirely on AI‑generated melodies, lyrics or vocals will be excluded from chart calculations. The policy aims to preserve the integrity of the charts while accommodating the growing use of AI tools in music production, and it will be applied to all chart‑eligible releases from the start of the next reporting week.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Libyan factions sign initial election pact amid institutional divisions
content:
Libyan political factions representing the rival eastern and western administrations signed an initial election pact on Monday, pledging to cooperate on a timetable for nationwide polls that could mark the first unified vote since the 2011 uprising. The agreement, brokered by the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) and witnessed by senior diplomats from the European Union and the United States, outlines a joint committee to oversee voter registration, security arrangements and the establishment of an independent electoral commission. Both sides said the pact reflects a “new political momentum” toward restoring constitutional order and ending the decade‑long stalemate that has fragmented the country’s institutions.

Nevertheless, analysts warn that the pact’s implementation faces significant hurdles. Libya’s two rival governments continue to operate separate ministries of interior, justice and defense, creating parallel security structures that could impede the safe conduct of elections. Moreover, the legal framework governing the electoral process remains incomplete, with unresolved questions about the constitution’s status, the legitimacy of the electoral commission and the criteria for candidate eligibility. The United Nations has urged Libyan authorities to close these gaps swiftly, but the deep institutional divisions and lingering mistrust suggest that the path to a credible, nationwide vote remains uncertain.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Angel Reese sets WNBA record with 26 rebounds in Dream win over Sparks
content:
Reese eclipsed a long‑standing benchmark in women’s basketball by surpassing Chamique Holdsclaw’s record of 24 rebounds, pulling down 25 boards while also contributing 11 points. The performance marked her 27th double‑double of the season, underscoring her consistency as a dominant force on the glass.

The rebound surge came during a recent contest in which Reese’s team secured a decisive victory, further solidifying her role as a key contributor. By breaking Holdsclaw’s mark, she set a new standard for rebounding excellence in the program’s history and highlighted the impact of her sustained production throughout the campaign.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Chelsea defeat Fulham 3-2 in London
content:
Chelsea opened the scoring within the first half‑minute of their London fixture, with Joao Pedro finding the net just 31 seconds after kickoff. The early breakthrough was followed by further goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer, each adding to the home side’s tally as the match progressed. The rapid succession of strikes put Chelsea in control early on and set the tempo for the remainder of the game.

The trio’s contributions helped cement Chelsea’s dominance in the encounter, allowing them to maintain a comfortable lead throughout the contest. Their efficient finishing underscored the team’s attacking intent and provided a solid platform for the remainder of the season’s campaign.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kremlin adviser warns UK drone factories could be targeted after missile blueprint transfer to Ukraine
content:
The British government confirmed on Tuesday that it will supply Ukraine with detailed blueprints for missile components manufactured in the United Kingdom, a decision discussed on the BBC Newsnight programme. The announcement follows a series of Western pledges to bolster Kyiv’s defence capabilities amid the ongoing conflict with Russia, and marks the first time the UK has agreed to share such technical designs directly with a foreign partner.

Officials indicated that the transfer of the schematics will enable Ukrainian manufacturers to produce or repair critical missile parts locally, thereby enhancing the sustainability of the country’s air‑defence and strike systems. The move has been met with scrutiny on Newsnight, where commentators examined the potential implications for both the UK’s defence industry and the broader security environment, while stressing the importance of safeguarding sensitive technology. The government affirmed that the hand‑over will be conducted under strict controls to prevent proliferation, concluding that the support aligns with its commitment to assist Ukraine’s self‑defence efforts.
author: BBC World

title: Lockerbie bombing trial delayed again ahead of scheduled start
content:
The trial of a Libyan man has been postponed for a third time after prosecutors disclosed new evidence related to a case that dates back 37 years. The delay was announced on Monday, following the emergence of the evidence three days earlier, which authorities say warrants further examination before proceedings can continue. The defendant, whose identity has not been released, has been awaiting trial for several months, and the repeated postponements have extended an already lengthy pre‑trial period.

Legal officials indicated that the newly uncovered material could significantly affect the direction of the case, prompting the court to grant additional time for both the prosecution and defense to review its implications. A new trial date has not yet been set, but the court affirmed its commitment to ensuring a fair process while balancing the need for a timely resolution. The next hearing is expected to be scheduled once both parties have had the opportunity to assess the fresh evidence.
author: BBC World

title: UK to use Ukrainian battlefield data to train AI for infrastructure protection
content:
London and Kyiv have signed a pioneering agreement aimed at protecting United Kingdom critical infrastructure from both domestic protestors and hostile foreign actors. Under the deal, artificial‑intelligence models trained on battlefield data from Ukraine will be deployed to monitor and mitigate threats to UK defence sites, rail networks and energy facilities.

The accord grants selected private firms access to the extensive dataset housed in Ukraine’s Avengers AI lab, enabling them to develop bespoke security solutions tailored to the UK’s needs. This marks the first time the UK has formalised such a partnership, signalling a new approach to national security that blends international intelligence sharing with commercial technology development.

By leveraging real‑world Ukrainian combat data, the initiative seeks to enhance predictive capabilities and rapid response to emerging threats. The collaboration underscores a growing trend of cross‑border cooperation in cyber‑physical defence, with the UK positioning itself to better safeguard essential services against both protest‑related disruptions and state‑backed attacks.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Washington Post ordered to reinstate columnist dismissed over social media posts after Charlie Kirk killing
content:
Karen Attiah posted a brief message on social media following the assassination of a prominent right‑wing influencer. In her post, Attiah stated that she would not display sadness over the death and went on to share excerpts of the influencer’s past remarks that were widely criticized as racist toward Black women. The comments she highlighted were part of a broader record of the influencer’s public statements that many commentators and civil‑rights groups have described as demeaning and discriminatory.

The influencer’s murder, which occurred in a high‑profile incident that has sparked national debate over political violence and free speech, prompted a swift reaction from Attiah and other activists. By refusing to express grief and by resurfacing the influencer’s offensive remarks, Attiah positioned herself as a vocal critic of the deceased figure’s rhetoric and legacy. The post has been widely circulated on social‑media platforms, drawing attention from both supporters and detractors who are debating the appropriate public response to the tragedy.
author: Euronews

title: France and Saudi Arabia to invest $7 bn in three Paris-area amusement parks, including a Dragon Ball Z park
content:
Paris, France – The French government and Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) have announced a joint venture to develop three new amusement parks on the outskirts of the capital, committing roughly $7 billion to the project. The plan, unveiled in a bilateral meeting earlier this week, includes a park themed around a popular Japanese manga series, marking one of the first major Western attractions to be built around the franchise.

Construction is slated to begin in 2025, with the parks expected to open between 2028 and 2030. The investment aims to boost France’s tourism sector, create thousands of jobs, and diversify Saudi Arabia’s entertainment portfolio abroad. The three‑park complex will feature a mix of thrill rides, family attractions, and immersive experiences tied to the manga intellectual property, alongside two additional parks focused on broader leisure and cultural themes. Upon completion, the development is projected to draw millions of visitors annually, reinforcing Paris’s status as a leading global destination for entertainment and leisure.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US deploys two carrier strike groups to Middle East, straining navy resources
content:
The United States announced the forward deployment of two carrier strike groups to the Middle East, a move that markedly amplifies American naval firepower in the region. The task forces, centered around the nuclear‑powered aircraft carriers USS Gerald R. Ford and USS Dwight D. Eisenhower, arrived in the Arabian Sea within the past 48 hours and are now operating in coordination with existing U.S. and allied forces stationed in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea. The decision follows heightened diplomatic and military tensions stemming from recent escalations between Israel and Hamas, as well as concerns over Iran’s naval activities and its potential to disrupt commercial shipping lanes.

U.S. Central Command described the deployment as a precautionary measure intended to deter aggression, reassure regional partners, and preserve freedom of navigation. The carrier groups bring a complement of fighter squadrons, maritime patrol aircraft, and a full complement of surface combatants and submarines, providing a layered defense and rapid strike capability. While the Pentagon has not specified any immediate operational plans, analysts note that the presence of two carrier strike groups constitutes one of the most concentrated displays of naval power the United States has projected in the Middle East in recent years, underscoring Washington’s commitment to maintaining stability amid the unfolding crisis.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Australia bans AI‑generated songs from official music charts
content:
A new policy introduced by the Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) this week will require any track that incorporates artificial‑intelligence‑generated elements to be clearly labelled as such before it can be eligible for inclusion on the official singles chart. The rule change, announced by ARIA’s board on Tuesday, aims to preserve transparency for listeners and maintain the integrity of chart rankings amid growing concerns that AI‑assisted productions could distort competition.

The decision follows a high‑profile incident in which a Sydney‑based DJ publicly acknowledged that his recent remix of Madonna’s “Hung Up” had been created using AI software. The AI‑enhanced version surged to the top of the Australian charts last month, prompting debate within the music industry about the role of machine‑learning tools in songwriting and production. ARIA’s new guidelines stipulate that any AI contribution—whether in composition, arrangement, or vocal synthesis—must be disclosed in the track’s metadata, and failure to comply could result in removal from the chart.

Industry observers say the measure provides a clear framework for artists and record labels while giving consumers insight into how songs are produced. ARIA will monitor compliance throughout the upcoming charting period and review the policy’s impact on future releases.
author: BBC World

title: Headlong: Microharness for Persistent Agents
content:
Headlong is a lightweight microharness designed to streamline the development and testing of persistent agents—software components that maintain long‑term state and interact continuously with external systems. The project, detailed in an update on Laude.org, offers a minimalistic framework that abstracts common agent concerns such as state persistence, fault tolerance, and lifecycle management, allowing developers to focus on business logic rather than boilerplate infrastructure.

The release notes highlight several core features: a built‑in persistence layer that supports multiple backends, a modular plugin system for extending agent capabilities, and a simple command‑line interface for deployment and monitoring. The tool has attracted attention on Hacker News, where its announcement received 12 upvotes and three comments, indicating early interest from the startup and open‑source communities. Contributors praised its concise API and the potential to accelerate prototype cycles for autonomous services.

In summary, Headlong provides a focused, easy‑to‑integrate solution for building resilient persistent agents. By reducing setup complexity and offering flexible persistence options, it aims to lower the barrier for teams seeking to deploy long‑running, stateful applications in production environments.
author: Hacker News

title: Data Centers Drive Rapid Expansion of Gas Power Projects in the U.S.
content:
The rapid expansion of data centers across North America and Europe has spurred a surge in natural‑gas projects, with dozens of new plants either proposed or already under construction. Industry analysts point to the growing energy demands of high‑density server farms as the primary driver, noting that many operators are turning to gas‑fired power generation for its reliability and lower carbon intensity compared to coal. In the United States, for example, several mid‑size gas turbines are slated to begin operations by 2025, while European utilities are investing in combined‑cycle facilities to meet the projected 30‑percent increase in data‑center electricity consumption over the next decade.

Key details of the boom include the geographic spread of these projects. In the U.S., new gas plants are clustered around major metropolitan hubs such as the Dallas‑Fort Worth area, the San Francisco Bay region, and the New York‑New Jersey corridor—locations that also host the largest concentrations of cloud‑service providers. European developments are concentrated in the Netherlands, Germany, and the United Kingdom, where data‑center operators are partnering with local utilities to secure dedicated gas supply contracts. These partnerships often involve long‑term agreements that guarantee a steady supply of power while allowing operators to meet regulatory emissions targets.

The broader context underscores a shift in the data‑center industry’s energy strategy. While renewable sources remain a long‑term goal, the immediacy of meeting current demand has led many operators to rely on natural gas as a bridge technology. This trend is likely to persist until storage and grid‑scale renewable solutions mature enough to support the high‑density, 24‑hour power needs of modern data‑center facilities.
author: Wired

title: Rare Tornado Strikes Carcassonne, France, Causing Damage and Injuries
content:
A rare tornado was captured on video as it tore across parts of southern France on Thursday, an event that has drawn attention from meteorologists and emergency services alike. The funnel, visible from a highway near the town of Nîmes, was estimated to be 200 meters wide and produced wind speeds of up to 120 kilometers per hour, according to the French Meteorological Service (Météo-France). While no injuries have been reported, several trees were uprooted and a few roofs were damaged in the surrounding villages.

Météo-France confirmed that the storm system responsible for the tornado was an isolated supercell that formed over the Mediterranean Sea before moving inland. The agency issued a tornado warning for the region earlier in the day, prompting local authorities to suspend traffic on major roads and to advise residents to seek shelter. Emergency crews are currently assessing the extent of the damage and have urged residents to remain cautious as additional thunderstorms are expected to develop over the next 48 hours.

The incident underscores the increasing frequency of severe weather events in Europe, a trend that scientists attribute to climate change. While tornadoes are uncommon in France, the country has experienced a modest rise in such occurrences over the past decade. Authorities remain on alert, and Météo-France will continue to monitor the weather patterns that may lead to further hazardous conditions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: France and Saudi Arabia approve $7 billion theme park near Paris
content:
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman concluded a multi‑sector diplomatic tour of Paris by signing a series of agreements that span energy, defence, artificial intelligence and tourism, including a new theme‑park project slated for development in Saudi Arabia. The deals were announced on Friday as part of a broader effort to deepen economic ties between Saudi Arabia and France, with the Crown Prince meeting French officials and business leaders throughout his three‑day visit.

Among the signed contracts, a French entertainment consortium will partner with the Saudi sovereign wealth fund to build a large‑scale theme park that aims to attract both domestic and international visitors. Parallel agreements cover a joint venture in renewable‑energy infrastructure, a defence procurement package involving advanced aerospace systems, and a collaborative AI research programme linking French tech firms with Saudi research institutions. French officials highlighted the projects as a boost to bilateral trade, while Saudi representatives framed them as key components of the Kingdom’s Vision 2030 diversification strategy.

The suite of agreements underscores a renewed momentum in Franco‑Saudi cooperation, signaling a shift toward high‑value, technology‑driven investments. Observers note that the theme‑park initiative, alongside the other deals, illustrates the Crown Prince’s focus on expanding the Kingdom’s non‑oil economy and strengthening strategic partnerships with European partners.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa thanks nation after removal from US terror list
content:
Syrian President Ahmed al‑Sharaa publicly thanked the Syrian people on Tuesday after the United States announced the removal of Syria from its State Sponsors of Terrorism list. The decision, made by the U.S. Department of State, marks the first time since 2020 that Syria has been cleared of the designation that imposes stringent economic and diplomatic restrictions on the country.

Washington’s move follows a series of diplomatic overtures, including Syria’s cooperation on counter‑terrorism measures and its pledge to curb extremist financing, as well as broader regional negotiations aimed at stabilising the conflict‑torn nation. U.S. officials indicated that the delisting reflects progress in these areas, though they emphasized that continued compliance will be monitored. President al‑Sharaa’s statement highlighted the perceived national achievement and signalled a desire to deepen international engagement, while analysts noted that the change could open pathways for increased foreign investment and aid, pending further reforms.
author: Al Jazeera

title: New Zealand sect leader jailed for death of Chinese follower
content:
A body identified as 70‑year‑old Shulai Wang was discovered near a marina on the outskirts of Auckland earlier this year. Police were alerted to the location after a passerby reported the find, prompting officers to secure the scene and initiate a formal investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death.

Authorities have confirmed Wang’s identity through forensic examination and are treating the case as a homicide pending further inquiry. Investigators are reviewing surveillance footage from the marina, interviewing witnesses, and coordinating with local forensic teams to determine the cause of death and any potential links to other incidents in the area. The police have asked anyone with information to come forward, emphasizing that the investigation remains ongoing.
author: BBC World

title: Airbound Raises $37M for Drone Delivery
content:
Airbound, a drone‑delivery startup, has secured new funding after unveiling an ultra‑lightweight design that promises faster, more efficient air couriers. The investment round was led by Greenoaks, the logistics arm of DoorDash, and Silicon Valley investor Lachy Groom. The partnership signals confidence in Airbound’s technology, which reduces payload weight and battery consumption, allowing drones to carry larger loads over longer distances while cutting operating costs.

The backing comes at a time when the drone‑delivery market is intensifying, with companies vying for regulatory approval and commercial viability. Greenoaks’ involvement brings DoorDash’s extensive last‑mile network and data analytics, positioning Airbound to integrate its drones into existing delivery ecosystems. Lachy Groom’s track record in scaling tech ventures adds strategic guidance, potentially accelerating Airbound’s path to widespread deployment. Together, the investors provide both capital and industry expertise, bolstering Airbound’s prospects of becoming a key player in the emerging aerial logistics sector.
author: TechCrunch

title: Projectile Strikes Oil Tanker in Strait of Hormuz, No Casualties
content:
A projectile struck an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz off Oman’s coast, causing damage but no injuries, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) announced early Tuesday. The incident, reported at 07:30 local time, involved a vessel carrying crude oil that sustained structural damage to its hull. UKMTO confirmed that the crew was unharmed and that the tanker remained under control, with emergency services on standby.

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint for global oil transport, and incidents in the area are closely monitored by international maritime authorities. UKMTO has urged shipping companies to maintain heightened vigilance and has requested additional information from the vessel’s operators regarding the nature of the projectile and the circumstances of the impact. No further casualties or environmental damage have been reported, and the tanker is expected to resume its voyage once inspections are completed.
author: France 24

title: Amnesty International alleges India used lethal weapons on protesters
content:
Amnesty International has accused Indian security forces of employing lethal weapons against demonstrators who were derogatorily referred to as “cockroaches” by officials. In a statement released on Monday, the human‑rights group said that police used live ammunition and tear‑gas canisters during a series of protests in the capital city, resulting in multiple injuries and at least two fatalities. The protests, which began on Saturday, were organized by a coalition of civil‑society groups opposing recent legislative changes, and participants reported being targeted after police officers publicly used the slur in a televised briefing.

The Indian government has denied the allegations, asserting that the force used was proportionate and that any casualties were the result of unlawful actions by a minority of agitators. A spokesperson for the Ministry of Home Affairs said an internal inquiry is underway and that the authorities are committed to upholding law and order while respecting the right to peaceful assembly. Amnesty International called for an independent investigation and for the immediate cessation of any use of lethal force against peaceful protesters, emphasizing that the allegations warrant urgent scrutiny by international and domestic monitoring bodies.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Netanyahu alleges Iran attempted to assassinate his son
content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu asserted that recent developments were a direct result of the joint United States‑Israel operation that targeted Iran’s supreme leader and four of his family members in Tehran. The claim was made in a televised address on Tuesday, where Netanyahu linked the alleged killing to a broader strategy aimed at curbing Tehran’s regional activities and preventing further escalation.

The operation, described by Israeli officials as a precision strike, was reportedly carried out by special forces from both nations and resulted in the death of the senior cleric, identified as a top figure in Iran’s political hierarchy, along with four relatives. The incident has prompted condemnation from Iranian authorities, who have called for an immediate response, and has drawn heightened scrutiny from the international community, including calls for restraint and verification of the reported casualties.
author: Al Jazeera

title: The hidden cost of high performance: New research questions 'win-at-all-costs' sport culture
content:
A review commissioned by Sport New Zealand and released this week has raised concerns that the nation’s high‑performance support framework may be contributing to adverse outcomes for some elite athletes. The independent inquiry, prompted by a series of high‑profile mental‑health disclosures and a recent increase in athlete withdrawals from major competitions, examined the structure, funding and oversight of programs that provide coaching, medical, psychological and financial assistance to the country’s top sportspersons.

The report identified several systemic issues, including inconsistent access to qualified sports psychologists, pressures linked to performance‑based funding that can encourage excessive training loads, and a lack of clear pathways for athletes to raise welfare concerns without fear of repercussions. Interviews with current and former athletes revealed instances of burnout, anxiety and depression that were not adequately addressed by existing support services. Sport New Zealand acknowledged the findings, noting that while the high‑performance system has delivered international success, the identified gaps require immediate remediation to safeguard athlete wellbeing.

In response, Sport New Zealand has pledged to implement a revised welfare protocol, increase the availability of mental‑health professionals, and establish an independent oversight committee to monitor compliance across all high‑performance programmes. The changes are slated for rollout ahead of the next Olympic cycle, with the aim of aligning performance objectives with robust health and safety safeguards for New Zealand’s elite athletes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Family medicine shortage: Why future doctors look elsewhere
content:
Dr. Genaro DeLeon, a resident physician at the Cleveland Clinic, is navigating a common crossroads in medical training as he evaluates whether to pursue a career in surgery or family medicine. The decision highlights a frequent consideration among clinical trainees who must align their professional interests with the distinct demands of different specialties before completing their residency requirements.

Cleveland Clinic’s residency framework provides structured rotations, clinical electives, and faculty mentorship to help residents assess their aptitudes across multiple disciplines. Surgery training emphasizes procedural proficiency, acute care management, and intensive hospital-based practice, while family medicine focuses on comprehensive, longitudinal patient care across diverse age groups and clinical settings. Residents typically utilize this comparative exposure, along with guidance from program directors and specialty advisors, to make informed career choices.

As Dr. DeLeon progresses through his training, his deliberation reflects the standard decision-making process embedded in modern medical education. Academic medical centers maintain flexible training pathways to support residents through such pivotal evaluations, ensuring that physicians ultimately enter practice in specialties that
author: Medical Xpress

title: CIA and Modern Art: Debunking the Psy-Op Theory
content:
JSTOR Daily’s recent feature, “Was modern art really a CIA psy‑op?” explores the long‑standing claim that the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency used avant‑garde art to influence public opinion during the Cold War. The article, which cites declassified CIA files, interviews with artists and historians, and academic studies, has drawn a modest online audience, sparking a discussion thread on Hacker News that earned 13 points and four comments.

The piece outlines how the CIA allegedly funded exhibitions, promoted American artists abroad, and leveraged modern art as a cultural weapon to counter Soviet influence. It also presents counter‑evidence, noting that scholars argue the agency’s involvement was limited and that the notion of a large‑scale psychological operation may be overstated. By situating the debate within the broader context of Cold War cultural diplomacy, the article highlights both the agency’s strategic interests and the complex relationship between art and intelligence.

In its conclusion, the article acknowledges that while there is clear evidence of CIA interest in modern art, the extent to which this constituted a coordinated psy‑op remains uncertain. The discussion on Hacker News indicates that the topic continues to engage a niche but active readership, underscoring the enduring intrigue surrounding the intersection of art, politics, and covert operations.
author: Hacker News

title: Thomson Reuters Launches Frontier AI Model
content:
Thomson Reuters announced on August 12, 2026 that it will launch a new “frontier” artificial‑intelligence model built on the company’s extensive, proprietary data assets. The model, which the firm says will be available to institutional clients by the end of the year, is designed to deliver advanced natural‑language processing and predictive analytics across financial markets, legal research and news distribution. By integrating its vast archives of market data, regulatory filings and real‑time news feeds, the company aims to provide deeper insights and faster decision‑making tools for traders, risk managers and compliance teams.

The launch follows Thomson Reuters’ recent investments in machine‑learning infrastructure and a partnership with leading cloud providers to scale the model’s deployment. According to the press release, the frontier model will support multilingual content, offer real‑time sentiment analysis, and generate automated compliance alerts. Industry observers note that the initiative positions Thomson Reuters to compete more directly with large‑language‑model providers that have entered the financial services space, while leveraging the firm’s unique data advantage.

Thomson Reuters expects the new model to enhance its suite of analytics products and expand its market share in AI‑powered financial services. The company’s leadership highlighted that the frontier model will enable clients to uncover patterns in complex datasets more efficiently, potentially reducing research time and improving risk assessment accuracy. As the model rolls out, the firm will monitor performance metrics and client feedback to refine its capabilities and maintain its reputation as a trusted data and analytics provider.
author: Hacker News

title: Haiti gang attack kills ~40 displaced people in church near Port-au-Prince
content:
A gang attack on Sunday night in Kenscoff, a suburb in the hills above Port‑au‑Prince, left roughly 40 displaced residents dead, a local mayor said on Monday. The victims were sheltering in a church when gunfire erupted, the mayor, Massillon Jean, described the event as a “night of terror.”  

Mayor Jean confirmed that the killings were carried out by gang members, though the specific group was not named. He added that several people remain missing, and local authorities are conducting a search. The incident follows a pattern of violence that has plagued the region, with displaced communities often seeking refuge in churches and other public buildings.  

The tragedy underscores the ongoing security crisis in Haiti’s capital area, where gang activity continues to threaten civilian safety. Local officials have called for heightened protection for vulnerable populations while investigations into the perpetrators are underway.
author: France 24

title: Reno Wildfire Evacuates 24,000 Residents as Smoke Threatens City
content:
A wind‑driven wildfire that has engulfed parts of Nevada’s Sierra Nevada foothills forced tens of thousands of residents to spend another night away from home. On Monday, the blaze pushed thick smoke over the city of Reno, prompting the closure of schools and the suspension of non‑essential services. The fire’s rapid spread, aided by strong gusts, raised concerns about air quality and the safety of nearby communities.

At the height of the emergency, more than 40,000 people were under evacuation orders. By Monday, that number had fallen to roughly 24,000, although the city still had tens of thousands of residents on alert, monitoring updates from emergency officials. Fire crews and the Nevada Department of Conservation and Natural Resources continue to work to contain the flames while authorities assess the risk to infrastructure and public health.

Officials say the situation remains fluid, with weather conditions and fire behavior dictating the pace of the response. Residents are advised to stay informed through local news outlets and the city’s emergency alert system as the situation evolves.
author: France 24

title: Gang attack on Haiti hillside community kills at least 30
content:
At least 30 people were killed in a gang‑led assault on a hillside community that commands the main routes leading into Port‑au‑Prince, Haiti’s capital. The attack, which took place in the early hours of the day, involved heavily armed gunmen who set fire to homes and opened fire on residents as they attempted to flee. Witnesses described a coordinated operation that targeted the densely populated settlement, leaving dozens of bodies among the rubble and prompting a mass exodus of survivors toward nearby towns.

The incident underscores the escalating wave of gang violence that has plagued Haiti since the collapse of the national police force in 2021, prompting the government to declare a state of emergency in several districts. Haitian authorities have dispatched additional security forces to the area and opened an investigation, while international partners have called for urgent measures to restore order and protect civilians. The death toll, which may rise as rescue teams continue to search the debris, highlights the fragile security environment surrounding the capital and the pressing need for a coordinated response to curb further bloodshed.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 29-year-old killed at Mexico's largest open‑road bullfighting event
content:
The world’s largest open‑road bullfighting event turned deadly on Saturday when a 29‑year‑old participant was fatally injured after a bull struck him during the run. The incident occurred amid a crowd of thousands of spectators who had gathered to watch the traditional competition, which is known for its high speeds and close interaction between riders and the animals.

Local authorities confirmed that emergency services responded promptly, but the man was pronounced dead at the scene. Police have launched an investigation into the circumstances of the crash and are reviewing safety protocols for future events. Organizers expressed condolences to the victim’s family and indicated that the event will continue under heightened supervision while the inquiry proceeds.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Muslims observe Mawlid al-Nabi in Iraq, Libya and Morocco
content:
Muslims across Iraq, Libya and Morocco marked Mawlid al‑Nabi, the observance of the Prophet Muhammad’s birthday, with public gatherings and religious ceremonies on Monday. In Baghdad, worshippers assembled at the Imam Ali Mosque for prayers and sermons, while in Tripoli, processions moved through the historic medina, and in Rabat, the royal palace’s courtyard hosted a series of Qur’an recitations and charitable distributions.

Organisers in each country coordinated the events in accordance with local regulations, emphasizing safety and community participation. In Iraq, authorities deployed police units to manage traffic and ensure crowd control, reporting no incidents. Libyan officials highlighted the gatherings as a demonstration of national unity, and Moroccan religious authorities underscored the day’s focus on spiritual reflection and social solidarity, noting that charitable donations were collected for families in need.

The celebrations reflect the continued significance of Mawlid al‑Nabi in the region’s cultural and religious calendar, drawing large numbers of participants despite varying security environments. Observers note that the coordinated, peaceful nature of the events underscores the role of the holiday in fostering communal cohesion across the three nations.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 68-year-old French tourist dies after car gets stuck in Death Valley mud
content:
A 68‑year‑old man was discovered deceased on a salt‑flat area in California on Tuesday, officials said, as temperatures in the region surged to 116 °F (46.6 °C). The body was found by a passerby near the expansive flatlands that border the Salton Sea, and the San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department was notified immediately.

County investigators confirmed that the death is being treated as a result of exposure to extreme heat, noting that the area’s reflective surface can rapidly increase body temperature under such conditions. The incident occurs amid a prolonged heat wave that has prompted statewide advisories urging residents to stay hydrated, limit outdoor activity, and seek shelter during peak temperatures. Authorities are reminding the public of the heightened risks associated with prolonged exposure in open, sun‑baked environments.
author: BBC World

title: Canada’s potential leverage in US trade dispute examined
content:
Canada’s economic ties to the United States—about 70 % of its exports flow across the border—give the country a complex mix of influence and vulnerability in the escalating trade dispute.  While the United States has used tariff hikes and regulatory pressure to push Canada to align on issues ranging from dairy quotas to digital services, Canada’s high dependence on the U.S. market means it must carefully balance retaliation with the risk of damaging its most important trading partner.  Consequently, Canadian officials have repeatedly emphasized the need for a negotiated settlement that preserves market access while addressing the United States’ concerns.

In practice, Canada’s leverage comes from its role as a key supplier of natural resources, automotive parts, and agricultural products that are integral to U.S. supply chains.  The country can threaten to impose counter‑tariffs or restrict imports of Canadian goods in sectors where the United States has less alternative sourcing, thereby creating a bargaining chip.  At the same time, Canada’s own domestic industries and consumers face higher costs if trade friction escalates, limiting the scope of punitive measures it can sustain.  The Canadian government has therefore pursued a dual strategy of engaging in diplomatic talks while preparing targeted economic responses to signal resolve without provoking a full‑scale trade war.

Ultimately, Canada’s leverage is constrained by its economic interdependence with the United States, but its position as a major supplier in critical sectors provides a limited but tangible bargaining power.  The country’s approach—combining diplomatic engagement with selective economic countermeasures—reflects an attempt to secure a resolution that protects both its trade interests and the broader North American supply network.
author: BBC Business

title: US Imposes New Sanctions on Iran, Warns Trade Partners
content:
The United States has issued a stark warning to countries that maintain trade ties with Iran, telling them to choose between supporting Washington or Tehran. In a statement released this week, U.S. officials said that any nation that continues to engage in commerce with Iran will face “consequences” that could include sanctions, trade restrictions, or other diplomatic measures. The message was aimed at countries in the Middle East and beyond that have historically traded with Iran despite U.S. sanctions.

The warning follows a series of U.S. actions aimed at curbing Iran’s influence, including the re‑imposition of sanctions on Iranian banks, shipping companies, and energy firms. Washington’s stance is that continued economic cooperation with Iran undermines its own security interests and the broader international effort to curb Iran’s nuclear program. Iran’s trade partners have reportedly been urged to reassess their economic relationships, with some already citing the potential for punitive measures as a reason to cut ties.

While the U.S. has not yet specified the exact nature of the “consequences,” officials have indicated that they could involve targeted sanctions on individuals and entities, restrictions on financial transactions, and limitations on access to U.S. markets. The move underscores the growing pressure on Iran’s allies and highlights the U.S. strategy of using economic leverage to isolate Tehran on the global stage.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ben Guerdane Protests Erupt After Migrant Boat Sinks, 12 Dead
content:
Tunisia’s southeastern town of Ben Guerdane has been rocked by violent protests following a maritime tragedy that left at least 12 people dead. The disaster occurred when a small boat carrying 15 passengers capsized off the coast near the town, prompting an outpouring of anger from local residents who blamed authorities for inadequate safety measures and alleged neglect of the area’s fishing community.

Security forces deployed to contain the unrest faced clashes with demonstrators, resulting in several injuries and the temporary closure of nearby streets and markets. Government officials confirmed the death toll and announced an investigation into the circumstances of the sinking, while pledging to improve maritime safety protocols. The incident has heightened scrutiny of coastal infrastructure and emergency response capabilities in Tunisia’s border regions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: DRC's 2028 Succession Battle Intensifies Amid Tshisekedi's Reforms
content:
Kinshasa – President Félix Tshisekedi’s accelerated reform agenda is intensifying a political contest over the Democratic Republic of Congo’s 2028 presidential succession. Since taking office in 2019, Tshisekedi has pursued a series of legislative and institutional changes aimed at curbing corruption, strengthening the judiciary and redefining the role of the ruling coalition. The reforms, which include amendments to the electoral code and the creation of a new anti‑corruption watchdog, have drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties and factions within the ruling Common Front for Congo (FCC), who argue that the measures undermine the balance of power established after the 2018 elections.

The dispute has crystallised around the selection of a successor, with the FCC’s former allies urging a consensus candidate while Tshisekedi’s camp promotes a younger, technocratic figure aligned with his reformist platform. Negotiations in the National Assembly have stalled as lawmakers debate the timing of the constitutional revisions and the eligibility criteria for future candidates. International observers have warned that a protracted stalemate could jeopardise the credibility of the 2028 vote and destabilise a country already grappling with security challenges in the east. As the deadline for candidate registration approaches, both sides appear poised to leverage the reform agenda to shape the next presidential race, underscoring the high stakes of Congo’s political transition.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US to revoke visas of 200,000 asylum seekers
content:
The Associated Press reported that a pending administrative decision could trigger the largest single mass revocation of visas in United States history. The action, which targets a specific category of foreign nationals, would involve the cancellation of tens of thousands of existing visas and the denial of future entries for individuals who fall under the newly defined criteria.

Officials said the measure is intended to address concerns raised by national security agencies and to enforce compliance with immigration regulations. If implemented, the revocation would surpass previous large‑scale visa actions, such as the 2020 suspension of certain diplomatic visas, and could affect travel, study, and employment plans for the affected groups. The administration has not yet set a definitive timeline for enforcement, and the policy is expected to undergo further review before any final determination is made.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Tornado injures over 40, destroys homes in southern France
content:
A tornado that swept through several villages earlier today left more than 40 individuals injured and caused extensive damage to residential structures. Local authorities confirmed that the severe weather event struck the rural area in the late afternoon, producing wind speeds strong enough to demolish homes and uproot trees across multiple settlements.

Emergency responders have mobilized to provide medical assistance, transport the injured to nearby hospitals, and set up temporary shelters for displaced families. Relief teams are assessing the full extent of the destruction, while officials have urged residents to remain vigilant for potential after‑effects and to follow safety instructions as recovery efforts continue.
author: BBC World

title: SpaceX to retire Falcon 9 after Starship becomes operational
content:
SpaceX announced that it will retire its Falcon 9 launch vehicle once the next‑generation Starship megarocket becomes operational. The Falcon 9, which has performed more than 300 missions since 2010, has been a workhorse for commercial, governmental, and international payloads, offering a proven mix of reliability and cost‑effectiveness. With the company’s focus shifting to the higher‑capacity Starship, the retirement of the Falcon 9 will reduce the number of available launch options in the market.

The removal of such a widely used vehicle is likely to tighten supply for customers who rely on the Falcon 9’s moderate payload capacity and established launch cadence. While other providers—such as United Launch Alliance’s Atlas V, Arianespace’s Ariane 5, and emerging players like Rocket Lab and Blue Origin—will continue to offer alternatives, the loss of Falcon 9’s competitive pricing and frequent launch schedule may prompt some operators to seek contracts with those competitors or to delay missions until Starship becomes fully operational. Additionally, the shift could accelerate consolidation in the launch industry, encouraging partnerships or shared launch services to maintain market stability.

In the long term, the transition to Starship is expected to expand the overall launch capacity and lower per‑kilogram launch costs, but the interim period may see a temporary contraction in available launch slots. Stakeholders will need to adjust their launch plans accordingly, and the industry will monitor how the market adapts to the departure of one of its most‑flown rockets.
author: Space.com

title: Chelsea's attack shines while goalkeeping remains unresolved under Xabi Alonso
content:
Chelsea’s recent outing left the club’s search for a replacement for Robert Sánchez still unresolved, even as the new front‑line trio appears poised to provide a temporary cushion for the manager’s evolving philosophy. After a weekend in which most of the Premier League’s title‑challenging teams exposed their own weaknesses, the Blues were expected to step up and keep the title race competitive. While they were far from perfect, the side’s attacking threat was undeniable, with Cole Palmer involved in all three goals and the team showing a dangerous quality in the final third, a performance that may have benefited from a first summer off in three years.

Defensively, however, Chelsea struggled to find cohesion. The midfield and backline were less convincing, with Josh Acheampong delivering an all‑action display that nevertheless could not compensate for the lack of solidity. The goal‑keeping position remains a persistent concern, a problem that has persisted since Thibaut Courtois departed. The new-look front three, while offering an immediate offensive spark, will need to be complemented by improvements in midfield control and defensive organization if the team is to sustain a credible challenge for the title.

In summary, Chelsea’s recent match highlighted both the potential and the gaps in the squad. The new front trio may buy the manager some time to implement his principles, but the unresolved issues—particularly the need for a reliable goalkeeper and a more cohesive defensive unit—will be decisive in determining whether the club can keep the title race alive and avoid a procession of results that could otherwise see the race dominated by a single team.
author: Guardian Sport

title: FDA approves new blood test for Alzheimer’s disease
content:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Roche’s Elecsys Phospho‑Tau blood test for diagnosing Alzheimer’s disease, marking the fourth Alzheimer’s blood‑based diagnostic test cleared by the agency in under two years. The approval, announced by Roche on Sunday, adds to a rapidly expanding portfolio of laboratory tools that aim to detect the neurodegenerative condition through a simple blood draw rather than more invasive procedures such as lumbar puncture or costly imaging.

The Elecsys Phospho‑Tau assay measures phosphorylated tau protein, a biomarker associated with the formation of neurofibrillary tangles in the brain. FDA clearance follows a series of clinical studies that demonstrated the test’s ability to differentiate Alzheimer’s disease from other dementias with a high degree of accuracy.
