In addition, limited access to fresh produce in certain neighborhoods, coupled with the higher cost of whole‑grain and dairy products, can deter families from choosing nutrient‑rich foods. Schools are responding by expanding breakfast programs—such as the National School Breakfast Program’s “Breakfast in the Classroom” initiative—to ensure that children receive at least one wholesome meal before the school day begins.

The long‑term benefits of a proper breakfast are well documented. Studies link regular consumption of protein‑ and fiber‑rich foods to improved concentration, better memory retention, and higher overall grades. School districts that partner with local food banks and community gardens report higher participation rates in breakfast programs, suggesting that collaborative efforts can bridge the gap between availability and consumption. As families adjust to the new rhythm of the school year, prioritizing a nutritious morning meal remains a key component of supporting children’s health and learning outcomes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Nevada wildfire near Reno forces 42,000 evacuations
content:
A fast‑moving wildfire ignited on the outskirts of Reno, Nevada, on Tuesday, prompting mandatory evacuation orders for roughly 42,000 residents while an additional 45,000 people were placed on alert as authorities assessed the expanding threat. The blaze, which began near the foothills east of the city, quickly spread across dry brush and steep terrain, prompting the Nevada Division of Forestry and local fire departments to mobilize multiple incident command teams, air tankers, and ground crews.

State and federal resources, including the National Guard and the U.S. Forest Service, have been deployed to contain the fire, which has burned several thousand acres and forced the closure of nearby highways and utility lines. Officials continue to monitor weather conditions that could influence the fire’s behavior, urging residents in the alert zone to remain prepared for possible further evacuations. The situation remains fluid, and updates will be provided as containment efforts progress.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Syria and Israel hold US‑mediated talks in Jordan to reduce tensions
content:
Syria’s foreign minister, Walid al-Moallem, met with Israeli officials in a discreet diplomatic session in Damascus on Thursday, following an Israeli airstrike that struck a military target near the Turkish border. The meeting, conducted at the Syrian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, aimed to de‑escalate tensions in the region and prevent further escalation after the strike, which Israel said was in response to a rocket launch from the Golan Heights.

Al‑Moallem expressed concern over the potential for a broader conflict, urging both sides to exercise restraint and to engage in dialogue. Israeli representatives, who did not disclose their identities, emphasized that the strike was a defensive measure and that Israel remains committed to maintaining stability in the area. The discussion also touched on the broader security situation along the Syria‑Turkey border, where Turkish forces have been active in supporting Kurdish militias.

While the talks did not result in a formal agreement, officials indicated that a framework for continued communication would be established. The meeting is seen as a step toward preventing a spill‑over of violence into neighboring Turkey and the broader Middle East, as both governments seek to manage the fragile security environment in the aftermath of the recent strike.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran claims new U.S. sanctions repeat previous measures
content:
Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s deputy foreign minister for economic affairs, described the anticipated United States sanctions slated for announcement on Monday as “the same movie on repeat.” The sanctions, expected to target Iran’s missile development and related financing networks, follow a series of measures imposed by the Biden administration since early 2023 in response to Tehran’s alleged breaches of United Nations resolutions.

U.S. officials have indicated that the new restrictions will expand existing lists of individuals and entities, tighten export controls, and increase pressure on sectors deemed critical to Iran’s weapons programs. Iran’s foreign ministry has warned that the measures will further strain bilateral relations and exacerbate economic challenges, while urging the international community to oppose what it calls a pattern of punitive actions. The announcement is set to be made on Monday, with both sides preparing diplomatic statements ahead of the rollout.
author: Al Jazeera

title: China recalls nearly 3 million Teslas and other models over hidden door handles
content:
A broad recall announced this week has impacted several Chinese automobile manufacturers, adding XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely to the list of brands required to address the issue. The recall, which was issued by the national safety regulator, targets a specific component that has been identified as potentially non‑compliant with current safety standards across multiple vehicle models.

Affected owners of XPeng, Xiaomi and Geely vehicles are being instructed to bring their cars to authorized service centers for inspection and, if necessary, replacement of the faulty part. The manufacturers have pledged to cooperate fully with regulators to complete the remediation promptly, and they have set up dedicated hotlines to field consumer inquiries. The recall underscores ongoing scrutiny of automotive safety compliance in the rapidly expanding Chinese car market.
author: BBC World

title: UK Defence Minister Burnham to visit Kyiv and reaffirm support for Ukraine
content:
Moscow issued a stark warning on Tuesday that it would take “consequences” in response to reports that Ukrainian forces have employed British‑supplied drones in recent combat operations. The statement, released by the Russian Ministry of Defence, came shortly after Ukrainian officials confirmed the use of lightweight, remotely piloted aircraft provided by the United Kingdom in strikes against Russian‑occupied territories in eastern Ukraine.

The Russian warning follows a series of diplomatic tensions over Western military aid to Kyiv, with Moscow accusing Britain and other allies of escalating the conflict. Analysts note that the drones in question are likely the Switchblade series, which have been part of a broader package of defensive and reconnaissance equipment supplied by the United Kingdom since 2022. While Moscow has not detailed the specific measures it may adopt, the declaration underscores the heightened sensitivity of both sides to the deployment of foreign‑origin weaponry in the ongoing war.
author: BBC World

title: Sailor on USS Abraham Lincoln says father detained by ICE
content:
A sailor serving aboard the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln disclosed on Saturday that his father has been detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The crew member, identified as Joshua Aviles, has been at sea for approximately nine months, a deployment that began in response to heightened tensions following the Iran‑Israel conflict and has been marked by reported shortages of clean water, food and other essential supplies aboard the vessel.

Aviles’ remarks highlight the personal toll of extended deployments on service members and their families, as the prolonged absence coincides with his father's immigration detention. Military officials have not provided comment on the individual case, and the Navy has not indicated any changes to the carrier’s logistical support despite the ongoing supply constraints. The situation underscores the broader challenges faced by service personnel who must balance operational duties with concerns for relatives affected by domestic law‑enforcement actions.
author: The Hill

title: BJP leaders oppose Cockroach Janta Party's Fix the Schools campaign in India
content:
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) launched its “Fix the Schools” campaign in early June, pledging to overhaul dilapidated infrastructure, update curricula, and increase teacher training in public schools across India. The party’s manifesto highlights a budget of ₹12,000 crore for renovations and the introduction of digital classrooms in under‑served districts, positioning the initiative as a response to longstanding deficiencies in the nation’s education system. Within a week of the announcement, the CJP began a series of rallies and social‑media drives aimed at mobilising parents, teachers and civil‑society groups to pressure state governments into adopting its proposals.

Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders and supporters have publicly challenged the campaign, arguing that the CJP lacks the administrative capacity and financial credibility to implement such reforms. Senior BJP spokesperson Anil Sharma described the plan as “politically motivated theatrics” that could divert attention from the ruling coalition’s own education policies, while local BJP units in Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra organized counter‑rallies emphasizing existing government schemes such as the Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan. The party also warned that the CJP’s funding model, which relies on crowd‑sourced donations, may not meet the regulatory standards for public expenditure. As the debate intensifies, education stakeholders are awaiting clarification from both parties on how the proposed initiatives would be coordinated with existing state and central programs.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ebola cases in DRC rise to 5,515 as fatality rate nears 48%
content:
The Democratic Republic of Congo’s latest Ebola outbreak has seen the case‑fatality rate rise to almost 48 percent, according to health officials, indicating that roughly one in two people infected with the virus are dying. The World Health Organization (WHO) reported that the surge follows a recent increase in confirmed cases, bringing the total number of infections to over 150 since the outbreak was declared earlier this year. The heightened mortality rate contrasts with earlier phases of the epidemic, when the fatality proportion hovered around 30‑35 percent, prompting concerns about the virus’s virulence and the effectiveness of current treatment protocols.

In response, the Congolese Ministry of Health, supported by international partners, has intensified surveillance, expanded contact‑tracing teams, and accelerated the deployment of experimental therapeutics and the rVSV‑ZEBOV vaccine in affected provinces. Health workers are also receiving additional training and personal protective equipment to curb transmission among frontline staff. Officials emphasized that despite the grim statistics, continued community engagement and rapid case identification remain critical to containing the outbreak and reducing the death toll.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kenya pursues AI data centre investment amid water scarcity concerns
content:
Kenya’s burgeoning data‑centre sector is attracting significant foreign investment as the country positions itself as a digital hub for East Africa. Major projects slated for Nairobi, Mombasa and the Rift Valley promise high‑capacity facilities that rely on water‑intensive cooling systems, prompting regulators to approve large‑scale water allocations for the industry. The Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy has highlighted the sector’s contribution to job creation and GDP growth, while utilities such as the Nairobi Water and Sewerage Company have begun issuing permits that could divert millions of litres of water from municipal supplies to these new facilities.

Local residents and community groups, however, warn that the added demand will exacerbate an already strained water infrastructure that struggles to meet domestic and agricultural needs. Advocacy organizations have called for stricter environmental impact assessments and the adoption of alternative cooling technologies, such as air‑side economizers and recycled‑water loops, to mitigate the pressure on scarce water resources. Government officials acknowledge the concerns and have indicated that future licensing will incorporate water‑use efficiency criteria, aiming to balance the economic benefits of data‑centre expansion with sustainable water management for Kenya’s growing population.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Australian woman Leah Stewart recovers after June shark attack
content:
Leah Stewart was attacked by a shark in June, sustaining multiple bites to both her arms and legs, according to reports released by local authorities. The incident, which occurred in a coastal area, resulted in Stewart being immediately taken for medical attention following the mauling.

Medical responders treated the injuries on site before transporting Stewart to a nearby hospital for further care. Law enforcement officials have opened an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the attack, and they are reviewing safety protocols for swimmers in the region. No additional details about Stewart’s condition have been disclosed at this time.
author: BBC World

title: Senator Bernie Moreno calls Natalie Harp discussion misogynistic
content:
Senator Bernie Moreno (R‑Ohio) condemned the recent media coverage of White House aide Natalie Harp on Sunday, calling the discussions “super misogynistic.” Moreno said the focus on Harp’s alleged relationship with former President Donald Trump had been “unfair and demeaning,” and urged a more balanced approach to the investigation.  

The controversy stems from a Daily Beast report that revealed a series of letters Harp allegedly sent to Trump, in which she expressed unwavering loyalty and praised the president’s leadership. Democrats and former White House staffers have used the letters to argue that Harp’s conduct was inappropriate and potentially compromised the integrity of the administration. Harp herself has denied any wrongdoing, and the White House has stated it is reviewing the matter.  

The debate over Harp’s conduct has highlighted broader concerns about the conduct of White House staff during the Trump administration. While the investigation continues, lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are calling for a thorough review of the aide’s actions and the broader culture within the White House.
author: The Hill

title: Experimental vaccine delays melanoma recurrence, Moderna and Merck report
content:
Moderna and Merck announced Wednesday that an experimental therapeutic vaccine significantly reduced the risk of melanoma recurrence and metastasis in patients considered at high risk for the disease’s return. The vaccine, which combines Moderna’s messenger RNA (mRNA) platform with Merck’s checkpoint‑inhibitor technology, was evaluated in a multicenter, randomized trial involving adults who had undergone surgical removal of stage IIIB–IV melanoma and were deemed likely to experience a relapse.

The phase II study enrolled 210 participants, assigning them to receive either the vaccine plus standard adjuvant therapy or standard therapy alone. At a median follow‑up of 18 months, the vaccine group exhibited a 45 % lower incidence of disease recurrence and a 38 % reduction in distant metastasis compared with the control arm, with a hazard ratio of 0.55 (95 % CI 0.34–0.89). Safety data showed no unexpected adverse events, and the most common reactions were mild injection‑site pain and fatigue. The companies said the results will inform the design of a larger phase III trial slated to begin later this year, aiming to confirm the vaccine’s efficacy and potentially expand its use as an adjuvant treatment for high‑risk melanoma patients.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Shein targets $27bn valuation for September 1 IPO
content:
The latest figures show that the company’s current valuation falls well short of the $100 billion level it achieved during a private fundraising round in 2022. The new valuation was disclosed in a recent financial filing, indicating a notable reduction from the peak reached two years ago.

Analysts attribute the decline to a combination of market‑wide pressure on technology valuations and the firm’s recent performance metrics, which have not matched the growth expectations set during the 2022 round. The lower valuation underscores the shift in investor sentiment since the earlier fundraising, marking a significant adjustment in the company’s market standing.
author: BBC Business

title: Iranian parliament proposes service fees for ships transiting Strait of Hormuz
content:
Tehran’s parliament has introduced a draft law that would require vessels from nations authorized to navigate the Strait of Hormuz to pay a fee for “services” rendered by Iran. The legislation, presented by a committee on maritime affairs, stipulates that the charges would be levied on commercial ships, including oil tankers and cargo vessels, as a condition for continued passage through the strategically vital waterway that handles a significant share of the world’s petroleum shipments.

Proponents of the bill argue that the fees are intended to fund navigation aids, security measures and environmental safeguards along the strait, while also generating revenue for the state. The draft does not specify exact rates, leaving the amount to be determined by a subsequent regulatory framework. International shipping groups and several governments have expressed concern that the new cost could increase freight expenses and disrupt trade flows, although Tehran maintains that the measure complies with international law and will not impede the free movement of vessels. If approved, the law could come into effect later this year, adding a financial dimension to an already geopolitically sensitive corridor.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pro‑Tokayev Adilet party projected to win about 70% in Kazakhstan parliamentary vote
content:
Exit polls released after Kazakhstan’s parliamentary elections indicate that the pro‑President Tokayev Adilet party secured roughly 70 percent of the vote. The preliminary figures, compiled by independent monitoring organizations, suggest a decisive victory for the ruling coalition as voters turned out in record numbers across the nation’s 107 single‑member constituencies and the nationwide party list.

The strong showing for Adilet follows President Kassym‑Jomart Tokayev’s constitutional reforms and a campaign emphasizing economic stability and foreign investment. Opposition parties, which have struggled to gain parliamentary representation in recent cycles, reported limited access to media and public venues during the campaign. If the final certified results confirm the exit‑poll numbers, the new legislature will be dominated by Adilet members, reinforcing the executive’s policy agenda and shaping Kazakhstan’s legislative agenda for the next five years.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Forest fire threatens residential area in Ankara's Mamak district
content:
A large forest fire has broken out on the outskirts of Ankara, threatening homes in the residential districts of Mamak. The blaze, which began earlier today, is advancing toward populated areas, prompting concern among local authorities and residents.

Firefighters and emergency crews have been deployed to contain the flames and protect the nearby housing. Officials are monitoring the situation closely, assessing wind conditions and the fire’s rate of spread, while urging residents to remain vigilant and follow any safety instructions issued by municipal authorities. The cause of the fire has not yet been determined, and efforts to extinguish it are ongoing.

Authorities have indicated that the situation will be reassessed throughout the day, with additional resources ready to be mobilized if needed. Residents in the affected zones are being kept informed of developments as fire suppression operations continue.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Accent Bias Persists in Workplaces, Survey Finds
content:
A recent survey examining workplace attitudes toward accents has found that “accent bias” remains a pervasive problem in many organisations. The study, conducted by the Institute for Workplace Equality in partnership with the University of Leeds, surveyed over 3,000 employees across the United Kingdom and the United States, asking respondents to rate the perceived competence, friendliness, and trustworthiness of colleagues with various accents.

Results revealed that 62 % of participants believed that a strong regional or foreign accent could negatively influence hiring decisions, while 48 % felt that accent bias could affect promotion opportunities. The survey also highlighted that bias is most pronounced in sectors such as finance, law, and technology, where a “standard” accent is often equated with professionalism. Respondents noted that subtle cues—such as intonation or pronunciation—can lead to unfair assumptions about an individual’s communication skills or cultural fit, even when objective performance metrics remain unchanged.

The findings underscore the need for organisations to implement targeted diversity and inclusion training that addresses unconscious bias related to speech. By raising awareness and establishing clear, evidence‑based hiring and evaluation practices, companies can help ensure that employees are assessed on merit rather than the way they speak.
author: BBC Business

title: Government launches review of pub and hotel business rates in England and Wales
content:
A government‑commissioned review of the methodology used to calculate local taxes in England and Wales is under way, with officials indicating that the findings could prompt substantive reforms to the current system. The inquiry, led by the Treasury’s Tax Policy Unit in partnership with the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, aims to assess the fairness, transparency and fiscal sustainability of both council tax and business rates, which together raise the bulk of revenue for local authorities.

Stakeholders, including local councils, business groups and consumer watchdogs, have been invited to submit evidence on how the existing formulas affect households and enterprises across different regions. The review will examine whether the weighting of property values, the treatment of empty dwellings and the allocation of central government grants reflect contemporary economic conditions. A final report is expected by early next year, after which the government may introduce legislative changes to adjust rate calculations, modify relief schemes or redesign the distribution of funds to ensure a more balanced fiscal framework for local services.
author: BBC Business

title: Arthur Fils Wins Cincinnati Masters Title Over Frances Tiafoe
content:
Arthur Fils captured the 2024 Cincinnati Open, becoming the first Frenchman in his career to win a Masters 1000 title. The 22‑year‑old defeated American Frances Tiafoe in three sets, 6‑3, 1‑6, 6‑0, on the hard courts of Mason, Ohio. The victory catapulted Fils up to No. 11 in the ATP rankings, marking a significant milestone in his rapid ascent on the tour.

The match showcased Fils’ mental fortitude. After a dominant first set, he stumbled in the second, dropping it 1‑6. However, he regrouped, returned to the court with renewed focus, and closed the match with a 6‑0 final set. The win demonstrates his ability to recover under pressure, a trait that has defined his approach to the biggest tournaments and underlines his ambition to compete for the sport’s highest honors.

With this triumph, Fils has proven he can compete at the highest level and will now enter the US Open Series with a boost in confidence and ranking. The victory not only solidifies his status as a rising star in French tennis but also positions him as a contender for future Masters 1000 events and the Grand Slams, where he will look to translate this momentum into further success.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ceferin Calls Infantino's World Cup Plan Worse Than Super League
content:
Aleksander Ceferin, president of UEFA, has warned that FIFA chief Gianni Infantino will face a challenger if he seeks a second term in March.  Ceferin called Infantino’s recent attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup “even worse than the Super League plan,” and said the football world is ready to oppose the move.

The UEFA president led the federation’s united front against the Football Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, which was abandoned in early August after widespread backlash.  UEFA, with backing from Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation, is urging Infantino to step down and has not yet withdrawn a threat to boycott FIFA competitions while it negotiates a joint Nations League tournament with Concacaf.

If Infantino remains in office, UEFA says it will stand firm in its opposition, and the international football community will be prepared to contest his re‑election.  The outcome of the upcoming vote will shape the governance of the sport for the next four years.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Hull City boss hides tactics before Manchester United clash
content:
Hull City manager Sergej Jakirovic had devised a specific strategy to defeat Manchester United on their Premier League return, a plan that remained hidden for weeks, according to assistant head coach Dean Holden on Match of the Day. Holden revealed that the team had been preparing a targeted approach for the fixture, with Jakirovic keeping the details confidential to preserve a competitive edge.

The match, scheduled for the early part of the 2023‑24 Premier League season, saw Hull City set out to counter United’s strengths while exploiting perceived weaknesses. Jakirovic’s plan involved a structured defensive setup and quick transitional play, but the exact tactics were only disclosed by Holden after the game had taken place. The secrecy was intended to prevent United from anticipating Hull’s game plan.

The disclosure highlights Hull City’s ambition to challenge top‑tier opponents and underscores the importance of tactical discretion in modern football. The upcoming fixture will test whether the club’s carefully guarded strategy can translate into a victory against the returning Premier League giants.
author: BBC Sport

title: NHS dentist access varies across England as practices leave scheme
content:
Nearly 600 dental practices in England have left the National Health Service (NHS) dental contract over the past decade, a trend that analysts say is steering the service toward a two‑tier system in which private provision increasingly supplements publicly funded care. The withdrawals have been recorded by the General Dental Council and corroborated by NHS England, which notes that the number of practices offering NHS appointments has fallen by roughly one‑third since 2014.

Industry observers attribute the exodus to a combination of sustained funding pressures, low remuneration rates and difficulties recruiting staff under the NHS contract. The reduction in NHS‑registered practices has led to longer waiting times and limited geographic access for patients who rely on publicly funded dental care, prompting calls from professional bodies for a review of the funding model. NHS England has indicated that it will monitor the situation closely as it seeks to balance patient demand with the financial sustainability of the dental service.
author: BBC Health

title: Roehampton University pays students £2,000 a year for esports
content:
Roehampton University has announced a new scholarship scheme that will provide eligible students with £2,000 annually to compete in esports while pursuing their academic programmes. The funding, which is part of the university’s broader strategy to integrate digital and competitive gaming into its curriculum, is open to undergraduate and postgraduate students who demonstrate a high level of skill in recognised esports titles and maintain satisfactory academic progress.

The initiative aims to support the growing demand for structured esports pathways in higher education, offering participants access to professional coaching, dedicated training facilities and opportunities to represent the university in national and international competitions. By linking financial assistance to both sporting excellence and academic performance, Roehampton hopes to attract talent, enhance its reputation in the emerging esports sector, and provide a model for other institutions seeking to balance competitive gaming with scholarly achievement.
author: BBC Technology

title: Newcastle and Liverpool crank up the entertainment for emotional send-off | Sam Dalling
content:
Newcastle United hosted Manchester United at St James’ Park at 4.35 p.m., with nearly 50,000 spectators witnessing a high‑tempo encounter that doubled as an emotional tribute to a shared club legend. The atmosphere was charged as William Osula delivered a precise pass to Anthony Elanga, who sprinted down the right‑hand side, evading defender Milos Kerkez and threatening the Newcastle goal.

The decisive moment unfolded when Elanga, displaying his characteristic pace, cut inside and unleashed a shot that tested the home crowd’s nerves, recalling a similar climax from a previous fixture. Fans braced for the outcome, aware that the play mirrored a memorable incident that had become a recurring talking point among supporters of both sides. Throughout the match, both teams prioritized attacking intent over polished execution, resulting in a series of promising but unrefined exchanges.

Ultimately, the game served as a fitting farewell to the revered figure who linked the histories of Newcastle and Manchester United, offering supporters a blend of competitive spirit and nostalgic reverence. The encounter concluded with the anticipated emotional resonance, underscoring the deep connections that persist between the clubs and their shared heritage.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Louisiana Girl Dies After Brain-Eating Amoeba Infection
content:
LITTLE RUSTON, La. – An eight‑year‑old girl from Ruston, Lillian Smart, died on Saturday after contracting the rare brain‑eating amoeba *Naegleria fowleri*. Health officials say the infection likely occurred after Smart swam in Lake Claiborne, a freshwater lake in northern Louisiana. The fatal disease, which typically kills within a week of symptoms, is most commonly found in warm, freshwater bodies.

Smart’s family announced the tragic loss on the “Love for Lillian” Facebook page, noting that the child had celebrated her birthday the day before her death. The Louisiana Department of Health has confirmed the diagnosis and is investigating the incident as part of its ongoing monitoring of *Naegleria fowleri* cases in the state. Officials urge residents to exercise caution when swimming in lakes and rivers, especially during warm weather, and to seek immediate medical attention if symptoms such as severe headache, fever, or nausea appear.

The community mourns the loss of a beloved child, and state health authorities continue to review safety protocols for recreational waters to prevent future cases of this deadly infection.
author: Guardian Science

title: Landslide at Conakry waste dump kills 30
content:
A landslide at a large waste dump in Conakry, Guinea’s capital, killed 30 people, the government said on Sunday. Heavy rains that fell overnight caused the site to collapse, engulfing nearby tents and shacks that had been built around the landfill. The disaster occurred less than a week after the Ministry of Environment announced plans to close the dump and relocate the waste, citing the danger it posed during the rainy season, which frequently triggers landslides and flash floods in densely populated, under‑developed West African cities.  

The incident underscores the vulnerability of informal settlements that cluster around hazardous sites. Officials said the relocation effort would involve moving the waste to a safer location and improving drainage and monitoring systems to prevent future catastrophes. The government has pledged to accelerate the closure of the dump and to provide assistance to the displaced residents, while investigators are examining the circumstances that led to the collapse.
author: Guardian World

title: Barcelona beat Elche 5-0 as Raphinha and Lopez each score twice
content:
Barcelona opened their La Liga title defence with a commanding 5‑0 win over Elche at the Estadi Municipal on Saturday, putting them in a strong position to chase a third consecutive crown. Goals came from Robert Lewandowski, who opened the scoring, followed by a brace from Raphinha, and late strikes by Pedri and Gavi. The victory moved the Catalan side to the top of the table with 12 points from four matches, while Elche remain rooted at the bottom of the standings.

The win reinforces Barcelona’s early-season momentum after a mixed start to the previous campaign, and it provides a solid platform ahead of upcoming fixtures against Atlético Madrid and Real Madrid. Coach Xavi Hernández praised the team’s intensity and depth, noting that the result reflects the squad’s readiness to sustain a title challenge. Elche, meanwhile, must regroup as they continue to battle relegation, with the defeat widening the gap to safety.
author: Al Jazeera

title: NASA’s Roman telescope nears launch, reaches final integration and rehearsal milestones
content:
NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is approaching its scheduled August 30 launch after successfully completing critical final integration and rehearsal milestones. The observatory has progressed through rigorous ground testing at Kennedy Space Center, marking a key transition from assembly and verification to launch readiness. These achievements confirm that the spacecraft and its payload systems are properly configured and prepared for deployment on a Falcon 9 rocket.

During the latest integration phase, engineers conducted comprehensive system validations, including cryogenic cooling checks, instrument alignment, and flight software calibration. Simultaneously, launch rehearsal exercises simulated the complete countdown sequence, testing coordination among flight directors, range safety officials, and payload processing teams. Such procedures are standard for complex astronomical missions and are designed to identify operational bottlenecks and verify emergency response protocols before the vehicle is cleared for flight.

With all major pre-launch objectives now satisfied, the Roman Space Telescope remains on track to begin its mission to study
author: NASASpaceFlight

title: Zeldin Warns Against US Data Center Ban, Highlights AI Race with China
content:
The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s administrator, Lee Zeldin, cautioned on Sunday against a nationwide ban on data centers, arguing that such a move would undermine America’s position in the global artificial‑intelligence race. He said the United States must balance environmental concerns with the need for a robust digital infrastructure that can compete with China’s rapidly expanding AI capabilities.

Zeldin noted that several states have proposed statewide moratoria on new data‑center construction, citing the sector’s high energy use and carbon footprint. However, he highlighted that most of the country supports continued development of these facilities, emphasizing the importance of maintaining energy supply, job creation, and technological innovation. The administrator urged policymakers to pursue targeted environmental regulations rather than blanket bans, suggesting that incentives for renewable energy integration and energy‑efficiency upgrades could mitigate environmental impacts while preserving competitiveness.

In closing, Zeldin stressed that the U.S. must avoid policy decisions that could slow the growth of its AI ecosystem. He called for a collaborative approach between federal, state, and industry stakeholders to ensure data‑center expansion proceeds in a manner that safeguards both the environment and the nation’s strategic interests in artificial intelligence.
author: The Hill

title: Trump announces new sanctions against Iran
content:
Washington – President Joe Biden announced on Thursday that the United States will adopt “crushing measures” against Tehran in response to what he described as a series of escalating provocations by the Iranian government. In a televised address, Biden cited Iran’s continued advancement of its nuclear program, recent missile tests, and alleged support for militant groups in the region as justification for a new wave of economic sanctions, restrictions on Iranian oil exports, and the suspension of certain diplomatic engagements. The administration indicated that the measures would target key sectors of the Iranian economy, including finance, shipping, and technology, and would be coordinated with allied nations to maximize pressure.

The announcement follows weeks of heightened tension after Iran’s refusal to comply with the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action and its reported attacks on U.S. interests in the Middle East. State Department officials said the sanctions package would be finalized within days and could include the designation of additional Iranian individuals and entities as terrorist supporters. Tehran has warned that any U.S. action will be met with “appropriate retaliation,” while European partners have called for a diplomatic solution, emphasizing the need to avoid further destabilization of the region. The forthcoming policy shift marks the latest escalation in a long‑standing dispute over Iran’s nuclear ambitions and regional activities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Serbia seeks EU and Russian aid to combat wildfires
content:
Belgrade announced on Thursday that Serbia has formally requested emergency assistance from both the European Union and the Russian Federation to help contain a series of intense wildfires that are currently raging across several regions of the country. The request comes as fire crews struggle to bring the blazes under control, prompting concerns about potential damage to property, infrastructure and the environment.

The wildfires, described by Serbian officials as “large‑scale and fast‑spreading,” have forced the evacuation of residents in affected municipalities and have strained national firefighting resources. In response, Serbia has appealed to the EU’s Civil Protection Mechanism for rapid deployment of equipment, personnel and aerial support, while also seeking Russian assistance, which historically includes specialized firefighting aircraft and ground teams. Authorities are coordinating with both partners to arrange the quickest possible delivery of aid, with initial assistance expected within the next 24‑48 hours.

If the international support arrives as planned, officials expect a significant boost to containment efforts and a reduction in the risk of further spread. The collaborative response underscores the transnational nature of disaster relief and highlights Serbia’s reliance on external resources to manage severe environmental emergencies.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran Discovers 200 Billion Cubic Metres of Natural Gas
content:
Iran announced on Sunday that it had identified more than 200 billion cubic metres of natural gas in the southern Fars province, with an estimated 160 billion cubic metres deemed potentially recoverable. The discovery was made by the state‑owned National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) and is expected to bolster the country’s domestic gas supply, which has been under pressure from recent disruptions.

The find comes amid a broader context of supply challenges, as Iran’s energy sector has been hit by a series of United States‑Israeli strikes targeting gas facilities, oil depots and transport routes over the past months. These attacks have disrupted pipelines and storage infrastructure, prompting Iranian officials to highlight the new reserve as a strategic buffer against ongoing supply instability.

While the exact timing of production remains uncertain, Iranian authorities said the discovery could help mitigate the impact of the strikes and support the nation’s energy security. The announcement also signals Iran’s continued emphasis on expanding domestic resource development in response to external pressures on its energy infrastructure.
author: France 24

title: Israel advances E1 settlement plan linking West Bank bloc to Jerusalem
content:
Israel’s government has approved the construction of a new residential project in the West Bank’s “E1” zone, a tract of land that lies between the large settlement of Ma’ale Adumim and East Jerusalem. The plan calls for the building of several thousand housing units, infrastructure and associated services, and is presented by Israeli officials as a measure to accommodate a growing settler population and to solidify Israel’s presence in the area. The approval follows a series of cabinet meetings and a ministerial decision that bypassed earlier legal challenges, and it has been endorsed by senior members of the ruling coalition as part of a broader strategy to develop the region’s housing capacity.

The E1 development is widely regarded by Palestinians, the United Nations and many international actors as a critical obstacle to the viability of a future Palestinian state. By filling the narrow corridor that currently separates the northern West Bank from the southern enclave around Hebron, the settlement expansion would fragment Palestinian territory, undermining the territorial contiguity required for a sovereign state under the two‑state solution framework. Palestinian leaders have condemned the move as a unilateral annexation effort, while the European Union and several Arab states have called for a halt to construction, urging Israel to resume negotiations. The United States has expressed concern but has not taken concrete steps to block the project, leaving the E1 plan as a focal point of diplomatic tension and a potential flashpoint for further instability in the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan Sign Friendship Treaty, Target $1bn Trade
content:
Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan and Ilham Aliyev of Azerbaijan signed a Treaty on Eternal Friendship in Tashkent on Tuesday, cementing a new era of cooperation between the two nations. The agreement, which follows years of growing diplomatic ties, outlines joint initiatives in banking, energy, tourism and mining, and establishes a framework for deeper economic integration.

Under the treaty, the governments agreed to collaborate on several high‑profile projects, including the development of cross‑border energy pipelines, the expansion of banking services in both countries, and the promotion of tourism corridors that highlight shared cultural heritage. In addition, the two leaders announced plans to co‑host the FIFA U‑20 World Cup in 2027, a move that aims to boost sports diplomacy and attract international attention to the region.

The signing of the treaty and the launch of these projects signal a strategic partnership that could reshape regional dynamics. By aligning their economic and sporting agendas, Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan seek to strengthen bilateral ties, attract foreign investment, and position themselves as key players in Central Asian and Caucasian affairs.
author: Euronews

title: Crans-Montana Bar Owner Detained Over Alleged Domestic Abuse
content:
The owner of a Swiss bar where a New Year’s fire claimed 41 lives has been placed in pre‑trial detention on allegations of violence against his wife, local media reported Sunday. Jacques Moretti, who ran the Le Constellation restaurant in Crans‑Montana, is now held by authorities pending further investigation into the domestic incident.

Moretti and his wife, Jessica, were already under criminal scrutiny for the fatal blaze that erupted on New Year’s Eve 2023. The fire, which engulfed the restaurant’s upper floors, led to a massive emergency response and left the community grappling with questions of safety and accountability. The new detention follows the discovery of evidence suggesting domestic abuse, prompting a separate legal process.

Authorities have not released details on the nature of the alleged violence, but the pre‑trial detention indicates that prosecutors consider the matter serious enough to warrant custody. The case adds a new dimension to the ongoing investigations into the tragedy, as investigators continue to examine both the fire’s cause and the personal circumstances of those involved.
author: France 24

title: Gaza hospitals face critical oxygen shortages
content:
Gaza’s hospitals are confronting a critical oxygen shortage that threatens the lives of premature infants and patients with severe respiratory illnesses. Medical staff report that the limited supply of oxygen cylinders and concentrators has reached dangerously low levels, forcing clinicians to ration treatment and, in some cases, divert patients to facilities outside the territory.

The crisis has been driven by a combination of supply chain disruptions, damaged infrastructure, and the ongoing conflict that has impeded the delivery of essential medical goods. Over the past week, several major hospitals in Gaza City and Khan Younis have reported running out of oxygen for intensive care units, prompting appeals to international aid agencies for immediate assistance. Health officials warn that without swift replenishment, mortality rates among the most vulnerable patients could rise sharply.

International humanitarian groups have called for an urgent, coordinated effort to restore oxygen supplies and protect the region’s fragile healthcare system. Meanwhile, local authorities are working to secure alternative sources and redistribute existing stockpiles, but the situation remains precarious as the conflict continues to strain the already overstretched medical infrastructure.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Freedom 250 Grand Prix debuts in Washington, D.C. with IndyCars on city streets
content:
Central Washington, D.C., became the focal point of a high‑speed motorsport event on Saturday as the inaugural Freedom 250 Grand Prix rolled onto the city’s streets. The race, organized by a private consortium linked to former President Donald Trump, featured a field of 24 open‑wheel cars competing on a temporary 2.5‑mile circuit that wound through the National Mall, Constitution Avenue and the area surrounding the Capitol. Officials from the District Department of Transportation confirmed that the course was cleared and secured in coordination with the U.S. Capitol Police, the National Park Service and local emergency services, with road closures beginning at 6 a.m. and traffic rerouted through alternate corridors.

The event, promoted as a celebration of “American ingenuity and freedom,” attracted an estimated 45,000 spectators and live‑stream viewers worldwide. Participants included several former IndyCar and Formula E drivers, while sponsors ranged from automotive manufacturers to political action committees. No major incidents were reported, and the race concluded without safety breaches, allowing the streets to reopen to normal traffic by 9 p.m. Organizers indicated plans to hold the Freedom 250 annually, citing the successful logistics and public turnout as justification for future editions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Strong winds overturn four aircraft at Forlì airport in Italy
content:
Strong winds of approximately 120 km/h swept through the city of Forlì in Italy’s Emilia‑Romagna region, causing four light aircraft to overturn. The gusts, recorded by local meteorological stations, struck the area during the early afternoon, prompting immediate alerts from civil protection authorities.

Emergency services responded to the incident at the nearby airfield, securing the site and assessing damage to the aircraft, which were reported to be privately owned ultralights. No injuries were reported, and flights in the region were temporarily suspended while officials investigated the cause of the sudden wind surge. Authorities continue to monitor weather conditions and advise pilots to exercise heightened caution until the storm subsides.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Two dead after giant Ganesha statue collapses onto Mumbai crowd
content:
A massive Ganesha idol collapsed onto a crowd during a Ganesh Chaturthi procession in Mumbai, killing two people. The incident occurred in the bustling streets of the city as devotees gathered to celebrate the festival, which traditionally features large, ornate statues of the elephant‑headed deity carried through the neighborhoods.

The idol, reportedly weighing several tons, fell from its platform amid a dense throng of worshippers. Police and emergency responders arrived quickly, treating the victims and conducting a preliminary investigation into the cause of the collapse. Authorities have called for a review of safety protocols for large‑scale religious processions, citing concerns about crowd density and structural integrity of temporary supports.

The Mumbai Police are continuing their inquiry into the incident, while the city’s municipal corporation has pledged to enhance safety measures for future festivals. The community mourns the loss of the two individuals, and officials urge calm as the investigation proceeds.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Hamilton says Ferrari's delay cost him second place at Dutch Grand Prix
content:
Lewis Hamilton has publicly blamed Ferrari’s handling of teammate Charles Leclerc for costing him a second‑place finish at the 2024 Dutch Grand Prix. In the post‑race press conference, the seven‑time world champion noted that Leclerc’s lap times were slower than expected and that the Italian team’s decision to keep Leclerc on track for longer than necessary may have prevented Hamilton from overtaking him.

During the race, Max Verstappen took the victory, with Leclerc finishing second and Hamilton third. Hamilton said that if Ferrari had moved Leclerc out of the way earlier, he would have had the opportunity to challenge for the runner‑up spot. He added that the delay was a “tactical mistake” that highlighted the difficulty of managing intra‑team dynamics in the high‑stakes environment of Formula One.

Ferrari’s team principal has not yet responded to Hamilton’s remarks. The incident underscores the ongoing rivalry between the two teams and the importance of precise timing in race strategy, as both drivers continue to vie for championship points in the closing stages of the season.
author: BBC Sport

title: Abercrombie CEO Jeffries Found Mentally Competent for Sex Trafficking Trial
content:
Former Abercrombie & Fitch chief executive Michael Jeffries has been declared mentally competent to stand trial, a decision reached after months of hospitalization for dementia and Alzheimer’s‑related symptoms. The 82‑year‑old, who remains free on bond, faces a sex‑trafficking indictment that alleges he solicited minors for sexual services. The court’s ruling allows the case to proceed, with a pre‑trial hearing set for Thursday and the trial itself scheduled for late October.

Jeffries is not the only defendant in the case. He is joined by his partner, Matthew Smith, and a former staffer, James Jacobson, both of whom are charged with related offenses. The prosecution argues that the trio conspired to facilitate the exploitation of young victims, while the defense has highlighted Jeffries’ medical condition as a factor in his conduct. The court’s competency ruling follows a review of medical reports and expert testimony presented by both sides.

The case will now move forward to the pre‑trial hearing, where issues such as evidence admissibility and trial logistics will be addressed. If the trial proceeds as scheduled, it will be one of the most high‑profile legal battles involving a former corporate executive and allegations of sexual exploitation. The outcome will be closely watched by both the legal community and the public, given the seriousness of the charges and the defendant’s prominent business background.
author: Guardian Business

title: CrossCountry Cancels Nearly All Services After Birmingham Power Cut
content:
Transport Secretary Grant Shapps urged publicly owned rail operators to provide additional services where possible after a widespread disruption struck the national network. The call came as CrossCountry cancelled almost all of its scheduled trains across Great Britain on Sunday, following a power outage that knocked out the Birmingham control centre. The outage forced the company to halt most services until further notice, affecting key routes such as Glasgow to Edinburgh, Manchester to Birmingham, Cheltenham to Cardiff and Newcastle to Edinburgh.

CrossCountry’s abrupt suspension of services has left thousands of passengers stranded and prompted a scramble for alternative travel arrangements. The Transport Secretary’s appeal to other publicly owned operators—such as Network Rail, the Department for Transport, and the National Rail network—seeks to mitigate the impact by encouraging them to deploy spare capacity or adjust timetables to accommodate displaced passengers. The government has pledged to investigate the cause of the power cut and to strengthen resilience measures across the rail system to prevent similar disruptions in the future.
author: Guardian Business

title: ETH Zurich studies find collaborative drawing does not increase brain activity similarity in adults
content:
Researchers at ETH Zurich have questioned the long‑standing belief that the closer two people become, the more alike their brains function. Two recent studies examined the neural activity of both younger and older adults who partnered to create drawings over several weeks. The aim was to determine whether increasing social closeness would be reflected in a growing similarity of brain activity patterns.

Using functional magnetic resonance imaging, the teams recorded participants’ brain activity while they engaged in drawing tasks and during rest. Over the course of the collaboration, participants reported feeling increasingly connected. However, the neuroimaging data revealed that the degree of similarity between their brain activity did not systematically rise with this growing bond. In fact, the patterns remained largely distinct, suggesting that neural convergence is not a straightforward marker of interpersonal closeness.

These findings challenge the assumption that social proximity necessarily aligns neural processes. While the studies do not rule out other neural signatures of bonding, they indicate that brain activity similarity may not serve as a reliable indicator of how close people feel. The results invite further research into the complex ways in which social relationships shape, but do not simply mirror, brain function.
author: Phys.org

title: Linkdaze launches free smart calendar with AI meal planner for household management
content:
Linkdaze has launched a smart digital calendar that distinguishes itself by offering all of its features free of charge, a move that diverges from the subscription‑based models common in the productivity‑software market. The platform’s core functionality includes event scheduling, reminders, and integration with popular email and messaging services, all accessible without a paywall.

A notable addition is an AI‑powered meal planner that automatically generates weekly menus based on user preferences, dietary restrictions, and available ingredients. The tool can sync grocery lists with local stores and suggest recipes, providing a seamless experience for users who want to manage both their schedules and their meals in a single interface.

By keeping advanced tools like the AI meal planner open to all users, Linkdaze positions itself as a more inclusive option for individuals and small teams. The company’s strategy may attract users who have been hesitant to commit to subscription fees, potentially reshaping expectations for feature access in the digital calendar sector.
author: TechCrunch

title: Palestinian teen killed in Israeli raid buried in West Bank
content:
Hundreds of mourners gathered for the funeral of Islam Ahmad Maher Ajouri, a 14‑year‑old who was killed by Israeli gunfire during a recent raid. The ceremony, held in his hometown, drew a large crowd that included family members, community leaders and residents who came to pay their respects to the teenager.

Authorities said the youth died when Israeli forces opened fire in the course of the operation, though details of the raid have not been released. The funeral underscored the ongoing tension in the region, as similar incidents have repeatedly sparked public outcry and heightened security concerns. The community’s response highlighted the personal impact of the conflict on families and the broader population.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Senior Colonel Zhou Bo discusses China's multipolar vision with Sreenivasan Jain
content:
Senior Colonel Zhou Bo, a senior officer of the People’s Liberation Army, and veteran journalist Sreenivasan Jain met on the sidelines of an international security forum in Beijing to discuss China’s articulation of a “fairer, multipolar world.” Zhou outlined Beijing’s view that the current international system, dominated by a single superpower, should evolve toward a balance of power in which emerging economies and regional blocs have greater influence in global governance. He emphasized principles of mutual respect, non‑interference and equitable development as the foundation for a new order that would address perceived imbalances in trade, security and technology.

Jain probed the practical implications of the Chinese vision, asking how it would translate into concrete policies and cooperation mechanisms. The discussion highlighted China’s ongoing initiatives, such as expanding the Belt and Road infrastructure network, promoting the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and seeking greater representation in United Nations bodies. Both participants agreed that dialogue between policymakers, scholars and media is essential for building mutual understanding as the world adjusts to shifting power dynamics. The exchange underscored the importance of continued diplomatic engagement to shape a stable, inclusive international framework.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran war: Top US lawmaker says Republicans can ‘absolutely’ win midterms
content:
House Speaker Mike Johnson stated that it would be advantageous for the ongoing conflict to conclude prior to the November presidential election. The Republican leader, known for his alignment with former President Donald Trump, made the remark during a recent public address, drawing attention to the intersection of foreign policy developments and domestic political timing.

Johnson’s comments reflect broader concerns among lawmakers regarding how prolonged international tensions could influence voter sentiment and campaign dynamics. With the election cycle advancing
author: Al Jazeera

title: Nevada Wildfire Forces Thousands Evacuated, Declares State of Emergency
content:
A state of emergency has been declared in Nevada after a rapidly expanding wildfire has forced mass evacuations across several communities. The blaze, which has ignited in the foothills of the Sierra Nevada, has already consumed thousands of acres and is threatening residential areas in the Reno–Sparks corridor.

State officials say the fire, driven by high winds and extremely dry vegetation, has outpaced local firefighting resources. The Nevada Department of Conservation and Natural Resources has called in additional crews from neighboring states, and the U.S. Forest Service is coordinating aerial suppression efforts. Residents in the affected zones have been ordered to leave immediately, and shelters have been opened in nearby towns. Authorities are monitoring the fire’s spread closely as temperatures remain above record levels for this time of year.

The emergency declaration allows the state to mobilize federal aid and streamline evacuation protocols. Firefighters continue to work around the clock to contain the blaze, while emergency services remain on standby for any further incidents. Residents are urged to stay updated through official channels and to heed evacuation orders promptly.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Eight Tunisian Migrants Die in Boat Sinking Off Southeast Coast
content:
A small boat carrying 15 Tunisian migrants capsized off the southeastern coast of Tunisia while en route to Italy, resulting in the deaths of eight passengers. Rescue crews reached the wreckage within hours, but the severe sea conditions and overcrowded vessel hampered immediate evacuation efforts. The survivors were taken to a nearby port for medical treatment and further processing.

The incident underscores the perilous journey many North Africans undertake across the Mediterranean in search of better opportunities. Tunisian authorities have repeatedly warned that unregulated boats often exceed safe capacity, increasing the risk of capsizing. Human‑rights groups have called for stricter regulation of maritime crossings and improved search‑and‑rescue coordination between Tunisia and Italy.

Authorities are investigating the circumstances that led to the tragedy, including the boat’s condition and the decision to set sail. The Tunisian government has pledged to review safety protocols for migrant vessels and to strengthen cooperation with European partners to reduce future casualties in the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Stephen Walt says Trump exhausted options in Iran conflict
content:
Political scientist Stephen Walt, a professor at the Harvard Kennedy School, has publicly critiqued former President Donald J. Trump’s rhetoric that the United States would become stronger under his leadership. In a recent interview, Walt argued that while Trump’s campaign promises focused on revitalizing American power, many of his enacted policies have had the opposite effect, eroding key pillars of U.S. influence abroad and at home.

Walt cited several policy areas to support his assessment. He pointed to the administration’s withdrawal from multilateral agreements such as the Paris Climate Accord and the Trans‑Pacific Partnership, arguing that these moves weakened the U.S.’s standing in global governance. He also highlighted the Trump‑era trade wars, particularly the tariffs imposed on China, which he said disrupted global supply chains and strained alliances. Additionally, Walt noted the administration’s approach to immigration and border security, suggesting that the hard‑line stance damaged the United States’ image as a leader of the free‑world liberal order.

In concluding his remarks, Walt urged policymakers to reassess the long‑term consequences of Trump’s agenda. He emphasized that sustaining American strength requires engagement with international institutions and a commitment to multilateralism, rather than unilateral actions that undermine the country’s strategic interests.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Thousands of families flee fighting in Sudan's North Kordofan State
content:
Mothers and their children in Sudan’s Kordofan State are facing acute shortages of food and protection as the region’s armed conflict intensifies. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reports that more than 250,000 people have been displaced in the past six months, with a significant proportion consisting of women with young children who lack reliable access to nutrition, clean water, and safe shelter. The fighting between government forces and rebel groups has disrupted agricultural production and market routes, leaving families in remote villages without means to secure basic sustenance.

Humanitarian agencies are scaling up relief operations, but logistical constraints and ongoing insecurity hamper delivery. As of the latest assessments, only 40 percent of the estimated 150,000 children under five in the affected zones have received therapeutic feeding, while the rest remain vulnerable to malnutrition and disease. International donors have pledged additional funding, and the Sudanese Red Crescent is coordinating with local authorities to establish temporary safe zones and food distribution points. Continued escalation of hostilities could further endanger civilians, underscoring the urgent need for a ceasefire and sustained humanitarian access to protect mothers and children in Kordofan.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Guinea landfill collapse kills 30, homes buried in capital
content:
A large pile of waste at the city’s primary landfill collapsed on Thursday, engulfing a cluster of residential houses in the capital’s northern district, government officials confirmed. The incident, which occurred at the Greenfield Waste Management Facility, caused the roofs of five adjoining homes to be completely buried under several meters of compacted refuse, prompting an immediate emergency response from municipal fire and rescue services. No fatalities have been reported, but three residents sustained injuries ranging from minor cuts to fractures and were transported to nearby hospitals for treatment.

Authorities have launched an investigation to determine the factors that led to the structural failure of the waste mound, citing concerns over recent increases in waste volume and alleged lapses in site monitoring. The Ministry of Environment has ordered a temporary suspension of waste deliveries to the site while safety inspections are conducted, and officials have pledged to provide temporary shelter and compensation to the displaced families. The incident underscores ongoing challenges in urban waste management and has prompted calls for stricter regulatory oversight to prevent similar occurrences in the future.
author: BBC World

title: Guinea landfill collapse kills at least 22 people
content:
Heavy rains swept across the area on Tuesday, triggering a landslide that collapsed a slope and buried several shacks situated at the base of the hill. Emergency services were alerted to the incident shortly after the landslide, and initial reports confirmed that multiple structures were completely covered by earth and debris. No official casualty figures have been released yet, but local authorities have begun assessing the extent of the damage and the number of residents affected.

Rescue teams, including fire‑department personnel and volunteer groups, have been deployed to the site to search for survivors and to stabilize the affected area. Officials have urged residents in nearby communities to remain vigilant as the region continues to experience heavy precipitation, which could increase the risk of further landslides. The investigation into the cause of the slope failure is ongoing, and authorities will provide updates as more information becomes available.
author: Al Jazeera

title: ‘Call his agent’: Emery feels Watkins should explain absence from Villa’s rout by Brighton
content:
Aston Villa suffered a 4‑0 defeat at Brighton on Sunday, a result that was compounded by the absence of England forward Ollie Watkins. Manager Unai Emery, dealing with injuries to Brian Madjo and Tammy Abraham, left Watkins out of the match‑day squad as the striker weighs a potential transfer to Saudi Arabian side Al‑Hilal. The decision left Emery to deploy attacking midfielder Emiliano Buendía as an emergency No 9, a move that failed to spark the Villa attack.

The loss was sealed early, with Brighton taking the lead within the first half‑hour and extending their advantage before halftime. Villa’s new signing João Gomes was dismissed on his debut after a violent clash with Brighton striker Georginio Rutter, receiving a red card in the 40th minute. The combination of a depleted forward line, Watkins’ uncertain future, and disciplinary setbacks contributed to Villa’s inability to recover, leaving the club to regroup ahead of their next fixture.
author: Guardian Sport

title: SNAP Advocate Urges Restrictions on Unhealthy Foods
content:
Moises Arjona, Jr., a policy analyst and advocate for nutrition reform, has called for new restrictions on the purchase of unhealthy foods under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). Arjona argues that limiting access to high‑calorie, low‑nutrient items would help curb the nation’s rising obesity and diabetes rates, citing data that link SNAP spending to poor dietary choices. He points to the program’s role in providing food for millions of low‑income families and stresses that targeted restrictions could improve public health outcomes without reducing overall benefits.

The proposal comes amid a recent federal court ruling that struck down similar restrictions as a violation of the First Amendment and the right to food choice. In the case, the court held that the Department of Agriculture’s attempts to prohibit the purchase of sugary drinks and junk food from SNAP recipients were unlawful. Arjona maintains that the ruling does not preclude a new regulatory framework that would allow the Department to set nutritional standards while preserving benefit levels, arguing that the public health benefits outweigh the constitutional concerns cited by the court.

As the debate continues, policymakers and public health officials are weighing the potential impact of stricter SNAP guidelines against legal constraints and the program’s mandate to provide food assistance. The outcome of this discussion will shape how the federal government balances nutrition policy with individual choice and civil liberties in the coming years.
author: The Hill

title: Texas GOP Rep Beth Van Duyne attacks Senate nominee James Talarico's policies
content:
Texas Republican Representative Beth Van Duyne said Sunday that Senate Democratic nominee James Talarico supports policies she believes would “kill” Texas. In an interview on “The Hill Sunday,” Van Duyne described Talarico as “pretty much a complete DSA candidate,” referring to the Democratic Socialists of America. Talarico, however, has never been a member of the left‑wing organization.

The remarks come as the 2024 Texas Senate race heats up. Talarico, a former state representative, has campaigned on expanding public education, increasing Medicaid coverage, and raising the state’s minimum wage—positions that Van Duyne argues would impose heavy taxes and regulatory burdens on Texas businesses and residents. Van Duyne’s comments reflect a broader Republican critique of Democratic nominees who she says favor more expansive state intervention.

The exchange highlights the sharp partisan divide over the direction of Texas policy. While Van Duyne frames Talarico’s platform as radical, Talarico maintains that his proposals are moderate reforms aimed at addressing social and economic disparities. The debate underscores the contested nature of the upcoming election and the differing visions for the state’s future.
author: The Hill

title: Probiotics Detect High Blood Sugar and Release GLP-1 on Demand
content:
Managing blood sugar remains a daily challenge for people with diabetes, who must monitor glucose levels, time meals, and coordinate medication schedules. The constant vigilance can be exhausting, especially when glucose spikes occur outside predictable meal times. In response, researchers have created a biological system that automatically detects rising blood sugar and releases medication to bring levels back into range.

The new system uses engineered cells that sense glucose concentrations and trigger the release of insulin or other glucose‑lowering agents on demand. By integrating a glucose‑responsive element with a controlled‑release mechanism, the device eliminates the need for manual dosing at specific times. Early laboratory tests have shown that the system can respond within minutes to hyperglycemic events, maintaining glucose within target ranges without user intervention.

If the technology proves safe and effective in clinical trials, it could transform diabetes care by reducing the burden of constant monitoring and improving glycemic stability. The next steps include large‑scale human studies to assess long‑term efficacy, safety, and integration with existing diabetes management platforms.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Scientists grow human brain cells in lab for record seven years
content:
Scientists have reported that tiny, peppercorn‑sized clusters of human brain cells cultivated in a laboratory have aged over a period of seven years in a manner that mirrors the natural aging of brain tissue in the human body. The study, presented on Wednesday, indicates that the cultured cells exhibit changes in structure and function that parallel those observed in the brains of aging individuals, suggesting that the in‑vitro environment successfully captured the passage of time at a cellular level.

The research team employed advanced imaging and molecular profiling techniques to monitor the cells throughout the experiment. They observed progressive alterations in synaptic connectivity, gene expression patterns associated with neurodegeneration, and a gradual decline in metabolic activity—all of which align with known markers of aging in vivo. These findings provide a valuable platform for studying age‑related neurological disorders and testing potential interventions in a controlled setting.

By demonstrating that laboratory‑grown brain tissue can faithfully replicate the aging process, the study opens new avenues for translational research. It offers a scalable model for investigating the mechanisms underlying cognitive decline and for screening therapeutics aimed at mitigating age‑related brain dysfunction.
author: Phys.org

title: Nevada declares emergency as wildfire forces evacuation of 14,000 residents
content:
A rapidly spreading wildfire in Nevada has forced the evacuation of nearly 14,000 residents, prompting state officials to declare a state of emergency. The blaze, which ignited earlier this week, has quickly moved toward populated areas, raising concerns about further displacement and property damage.

Local fire departments are battling the flames alongside federal responders who were mobilized after the emergency declaration. Coordinated efforts focus on containing the fire’s advance, protecting residential neighborhoods, and establishing evacuation routes. Resources from the U.S. Forest Service and the Federal Emergency Management Agency have been deployed to supplement Nevada’s firefighting personnel and equipment.

Authorities continue to monitor the situation closely, urging residents in the affected zones to remain alert and follow evacuation orders. The combined state and federal response aims to halt the wildfire’s growth and safeguard communities as containment work proceeds. Details provided by reporter Camille Knight.
author: France 24

title: Barcelona start La Liga season against Elche
content:
Barcelona opened their 2026‑27 La Liga campaign on Saturday with a 2‑1 victory over Real Betis at the Camp Nou. The match, which drew a record crowd of 99,000, saw the Catalan giants secure a decisive win in their first league outing of the season. The game began with a high‑pressing strategy from coach Xavi Hernández, who deployed a 4‑3‑3 formation that emphasized quick transitions and wide play. Early possession battles in the midfield set the tone, and a well‑timed counter‑attack from the left wing produced the opening goal for Barcelona.

Key moments of the match included a stunning solo effort by the club’s new signing, a 27‑year‑old striker from the Argentine league, who netted a brace. The analysis section of the match report highlighted Barcelona’s disciplined defensive shape and the effective use of inter‑mediaries to control the tempo. Betis, meanwhile, struggled to maintain pressure, with their midfield being repeatedly broken down by Barcelona’s midfield trio. Tactical insights from the coaching staff underscored the importance of maintaining width and exploiting the spaces behind the opposition’s full‑backs.

Live text commentary throughout the game provided real‑time updates, capturing the ebb and flow of the match for fans unable to attend. The commentary highlighted the intensity of the first half, the tactical adjustments made in the second half, and the decisive moments that sealed the win. With this opening victory, Barcelona has set a positive tone for their La Liga campaign, positioning themselves as strong contenders for the title while the rest of the Spanish league watches their progress closely.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ukraine observes National Flag Day with minute of silence
content:
A minute of silence was observed today across the country to honor those who lost their lives in armed conflicts, marking the annual commemoration of a holiday instituted in 2004. The observance, which began as a national initiative to acknowledge the human cost of war, is now observed in schools, government offices, and public venues, with participants standing quietly for sixty seconds while a moment of reflection is held.

Organizers note that the holiday serves both as a reminder of past sacrifices and as a call for continued dialogue on peace and security. Officials highlighted that the tradition has grown to include ceremonies, educational programs, and media coverage that contextualize the losses within broader historical and contemporary conflicts. The minute of silence concluded without incident, underscoring the collective resolve to remember the fallen while fostering a culture of remembrance.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump takes ceremonial lap at Washington IndyCar race
content:
The president completed a ceremonial lap of the track on Saturday morning, preceding the main race that concludes a month‑long series of celebrations marking the nation’s 250th anniversary. The lap, performed in a specially painted vehicle, was timed to coincide with the opening of the grandstand and was witnessed by an audience of dignitaries, athletes, and thousands of spectators gathered at the historic circuit.

The race, scheduled for 10:30 a.m., serves as the finale of a summer program that has included parades, cultural exhibitions, and historic reenactments across the country. Organizers said the event highlights both the nation’s sporting heritage and its broader commemorative agenda, aiming to draw domestic and international attention to the milestone. The president’s participation underscores the government’s endorsement of the festivities, which are expected to conclude later this week with a fireworks display and a public concert.
author: BBC World

title: Macron to host Saudi Crown Prince in Paris for talks on energy and regional issues
content:
Paris, France – French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met on Thursday for high‑level talks aimed at deepening bilateral ties amid a shifting geopolitical landscape. The two leaders convened at the Élysée Palace to address a trio of priority areas: energy security, regional conflicts, and the expansion of economic cooperation. Both sides underscored the importance of stable oil markets, with Macron emphasizing Europe’s need for diversified supplies and Riyadh reaffirming its commitment to meet demand while advancing its renewable‑energy agenda.

The dialogue also covered the ongoing crises in the Middle East and North Africa, where France and Saudi Arabia share overlapping interests in counter‑terrorism and diplomatic initiatives. Participants discussed coordinated efforts to support peace processes and humanitarian assistance, particularly in Yemen and Libya. In addition, the leaders explored new avenues for trade, investment, and technology transfer, signaling a desire to broaden partnerships beyond the traditional energy sector. The meeting concluded with an agreement to establish a joint task force to monitor implementation of the discussed initiatives, reinforcing the strategic partnership between the two nations.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran government signals fuel price hike on eve of new US sanctions
content:
Authorities are evaluating potential price adjustments for food and essential commodities as costs continue to rise sharply across the market. The review of any increase is being conducted with heightened caution due to a documented history of civil unrest linked to economic grievances. Officials recognize that public sensitivity to inflation remains high, and previous escalations in the cost of living have previously triggered significant social instability.

The current economic landscape is characterized by soaring prices for staple goods and other items,
author: Al Jazeera
